Built route x method x auth-dep x limiter x flag-gate (dumps in scratchpad/route_table.{txt,json}, decorator map in decos.txt). Auth-dep census: verify_admin_key 19, get_current_user 25, get_optional_user 8 (+_require_referral_enabled 4), NO auth dep 20 (legal x4, url x7, text/quick, text/prices, share GET, version, /, /favicon, /health, auth login/register/refresh/password-reset/social-login/resend-verification). Limiter census: 62 routes carry @limiter.limit, 20 do not, and SlowAPIMiddleware is OFF (ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS absent from Railway -> default "" -> falsy), so those 20 are unmetered today (confirms LS-ratelimit-02 still-open). Read in full at HEAD: home_routes(875), profile_routes(558), admin_routes(879), share_routes, legal_routes, version_routes, usage_routes, feedback_routes, history_routes, referral_routes, image_routes, url_routes, main.py + _AdminAuthenticatedStaticFiles, security.py, error_handler.py, sentry_service.py, url_validator.py, auth_service.py verify/logout/cascade, database_service history+share paths. SSRF: url_validator probed against 20 URL forms (loopback, link-local/169.254.169.254, ::1, IPv4-mapped v6, decimal/octal/hex integer hosts, 127.1, TEST-NET, CGNAT, multicast, odd ports) - obfuscated forms all correctly blocked; enumerated all 19 validate_external_url call sites and all curl_fetch_html vs curl_fetch_html_same_site sites. SECRETS/ENV: cross-checked all 54 Railway `web` variable NAMES (+53 on price-warmer) against a regex sweep of every os.getenv/os.environ read in app/ and scripts/, three ways (dead-in-Railway, silent-default-absent-from-Railway, reachable-by-logs/Sentry); scratchpad/envscan.txt. Sentry `_before_send` executed against a synthetic event covering 12 event regions with a real-shaped JWT and an admin key - produced a measured leak map. pip-audit -r requirements.txt --strict in a throwaway venv: EXIT 0, "No known vulnerabilities found" (the clean claim HOLDS at HEAD). DB EXPOSURE: scanned all 30 migrations for ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY / CREATE POLICY / GRANT / REVOKE / SECURITY DEFINER / views; enumerated 4 SECURITY DEFINER functions (delete_user_cascade, increment_lifetime_comparisons, resolve_referral_code, home_savings_aggregate) + 3 cohort views + 1 live function with no migration (cleanup_expired_ratings); then probed the LIVE database read-only with both the anon key and the service key across 23 tables + 4 RPCs (exact row counts via Prefer: count=exact, Range 0-0) and a GET-on-volatile-RPC privilege probe that cannot execute a write. Confirmed SUPABASE_ANON_KEY / SUPABASE_URL / createClient have ZERO references in SmartCompareApp/src or App.tsx (the anon key does NOT ship in the mobile bundle today). Also checked: backend/ shadow app (37 git-tracked files, own Procfile+railway.json), JWT verify/revocation path, X-Device-Fingerprint trust, delete_user_cascade completeness vs the live table list, prompt-injection boundary on extract_specs_targeted. Prod touched with exactly 6 GETs (health, admin/costs, openapi.json, docs, admin/cohort.html, admin/) - no writes anywhere.
cr-security.not_covered: (1) LIVE WRITE-PATH RLS (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies on the 23 tables) was NOT probed - HARD RULE 1 forbids writing to prod Supabase, so write exposure (incl. the L2 cache-poisoning path) is reported from migration source + read-side evidence only. (2) For the same reason I did NOT fire the two proven single-request exploits at prod: the anon POST /rpc/delete_user_cascade (destructive) and the non-ASCII X-Admin-Key request (it would itself exfiltrate the real ADMIN_API_KEY into the production Sentry project - firing it would cause the harm I am reporting). Both are proven by a read-only privilege probe / local reproduction instead; see the two findings' repro fields. (3) Supabase dashboard-level settings are unreadable from here: actual JWT expiry (the 3600s blacklist TTL assumes 1h), "Skip nonce checks", and whether an extra permissive policy (vs RLS simply being off) explains the user_events read - the effect is measured either way. (4) Railway secret VALUES were never read (only names, from the supplied baseline), so I cannot say whether CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is still valid at Cloudflare - only that nothing in the repo reads it. (5) auth_routes.py and text_routes.py internals beyond the auth dependency + the two unmetered handlers - owned by the M13/M18 lanes; I did not re-review register/login/refresh bodies. (6) Column drift and migration-application state per table - owned by cr-data-migrations; I report only policy/grant exposure. (7) No rate-limit brute-force measurement of the /admin/*.html Basic-auth mount (it carries no limiter and SlowAPIMiddleware is off, so it is unmetered - stated, not measured, since measuring means hammering prod). (8) Mobile-side Sentry (MB-security-01/02) and mobile secret storage - MB lane. (9) The 3 cohort views' write side and migrations/rollback/*.sql. (10) No CI run; backend pytest was not run at all in this lane (nothing here needed the off-lock local env).

findings.title: The Supabase anon role holds EXECUTE on delete_user_cascade: one unauthenticated POST wipes any user's entire account data by UUID
findings.evidence: Read-only privilege probe, anon key: GET /rest/v1/rpc/delete_user_cascade?target_user_id=<uuid> -> 405 {"code":"25006","message":"cannot execute DELETE in a read-only transaction"}. A role WITHOUT execute gets 404/PGRST202 (control: rpc/m22_definitely_not_a_function -> 404 PGRST202). 25006 means the SECURITY DEFINER body STARTED running as anon.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/p7.py (read-only): anon GET on rpc/delete_user_cascade, rpc/increment_lifetime_comparisons, rpc/cleanup_expired_ratings all return 405/25006 (= EXECUTE granted, body entered, only PostgREST's read-only GET transaction stopped it); unknown-function control returns 404/PGRST202. The POST form runs read-write. I deliberately did NOT send the POST. Owner-side confirmation: SELECT has_function_privilege('anon','public.delete_user_cascade(uuid)','EXECUTE');
findings.impact: Any holder of the Supabase anon key can permanently destroy ANY user's data - user_events, comparison_feedback, comparisons, search_logs, user_usage, referral_invites, referral_redemptions - and null their preferences/behavior_profile/push token, with no auth and no rate limit, addressing users purely by UUID. increment_lifetime_comparisons lets the same caller burn any user's free-tier quota to zero. cleanup_expired_ratings is a third anon-callable DELETE. The victim UUIDs are handed over by the same key via CR-SECURITY-02 (7 real user_ids measured), so the chain needs no guessing. Blast radius today = all 18 users. Migrations 010:70 and 011:61 create these functions with no REVOKE, so Postgres's default EXECUTE-to-PUBLIC grant stands; migration 036:94 proves the team knows the fix ('REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION ... FROM PUBLIC; GRANT EXECUTE ... TO authenticated, service_role') but never retro-fitted the older three. Mitigation today, not a control: the anon key has zero references in SmartCompareApp/src, so it is not in the shipped bundle - but a Supabase anon key is by design a public credential and one direct-Supabase client publishes it.
findings.fix: Ship a migration 037 that does, for each of the three: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.delete_user_cascade(uuid) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated; GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role; (delete_user_cascade and cleanup_expired_ratings are called only by the service-role admin client - database_service.py:157 - so service_role alone is sufficient; increment_lifetime_comparisons should get service_role only too). Then add the cross-tenant guard that 036 already models (AND (auth.uid() = target_user_id OR coalesce(auth.role(),'') = 'service_role')) as defence in depth, and add a repo rule that every CREATE FUNCTION ... SECURITY DEFINER must be followed by an explicit REVOKE/GRANT pair. No feature flag - this is a grant, apply it directly. Note migrations 033-036 are still UNAPPLIED, so 037 must be sequenced with them.
findings.test_first: tests/test_security_definer_grants.py: (a) a source test that parses every migrations/*.sql, collects each 'SECURITY DEFINER' function name, and asserts a matching 'REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION <name>' appears in the same or a later migration - RED today for delete_user_cascade + increment_lifetime_comparisons; (b) a live_db-marked test that asserts has_function_privilege('anon', fn, 'EXECUTE') is false for every SECURITY DEFINER function.
findings.dedupe: new (adjacent to known:M18/CD-db-rls-06 'resolve_referral_code SECURITY DEFINER granted to anon returns the referrer's UUID' - P3, read-only, and explicitly GRANTed by design at 014:102. This is the destructive-write half of the same class and was never filed: 010/011 have no GRANT line at all, so nobody looked.)

findings.title: user_events RLS is not in effect in prod: the anon key reads all 146 rows including 7 real user UUIDs, comparison_ids and event_data
findings.evidence: migrations/010:58 'CREATE POLICY events_select ON user_events FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id)' -> anon must see 0. LIVE: anon GET /rest/v1/user_events -> 206, content-range 0-0/146; service_role -> 0-0/146. Identical. Filtered user_id=not.is.null: anon 146, service 146. Row keys: comparison_id, created_at, event_data, event_type, id, session_id, user_id.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/rpc_probe3.py + p5.py (SELECT-only, anon key from .env): GET {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/user_events?select=*&limit=1 with the anon apikey returns a row carrying a non-null user_id; the Prefer:count=exact probe returns 146 for anon and 146 for service_role. Contrast controls that ARE enforced: users 0/18, search_logs 0/16283, admin_audit_log 0/1439, comparison_feedback 0/1 - so the anon key is valid and RLS works elsewhere.
findings.impact: Every product-analytics row is world-readable to any anon-key holder: 7 distinct real user UUIDs, their comparison_ids, and the full event_data blob (onboarding_started/completed/step_completed, compare_entry_paywall_banner_view/tap, comparison_completed, result_view_duration). That is a per-user behavioural profile plus - critically - the exact user_id list an attacker needs to aim CR-SECURITY-01's delete_user_cascade. It also means migration 010 is NOT the live truth for this table: either ALTER TABLE user_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (010:12) never took, or a permissive policy was added out-of-band. Volume is small today (146 rows / 18 users) only because traffic is ~0; it grows linearly with launch.
findings.fix: Verify and repair live state, then pin it: run 'ALTER TABLE public.user_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE public.user_events FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;' and drop any policy other than events_insert/events_select as written in 010:56-59, in a new migration 037 alongside the CR-SECURITY-01 revokes. Because the app writes user_events through the service-role client (feedback_service track_events_batch), FORCE RLS does not break the write path only if service_role is exempt - it is (BYPASSRLS), so verify with a live_db test rather than assuming. Do the same audit for every table 010 claims to protect - this drift was invisible because nothing compares the migration to the live catalog.
findings.test_first: tests/test_rls_live_matrix.py (live_db marker): for each of the 23 live tables, issue a count=exact SELECT with the anon key and with the service key and assert the anon count matches the documented matrix (0 for users/search_logs/user_events/comparison_feedback/user_usage/admin_audit_log/referral_*). RED today on user_events (146 vs expected 0).
findings.dedupe: new (M18's CD-db-rls-02/03/04 covered admin_audit_log INSERT, the L2 cache tables and the cohort views - all from migration SOURCE. Nobody had queried the live DB as anon, so this table's drift from its own migration was never seen.)

findings.title: Sentry _before_send scrubs 5 of 12 event regions: stack-frame locals, request body, cookies, extra, contexts and logentry all ship secrets unredacted
findings.evidence: Ran _before_send on a synthetic event. Surviving leaks: .exception.values[0].stacktrace.frames[*].vars.token / .vars.authorization / .vars.x_admin_key / .vars.expected, .request.data.access_token, .request.cookies.session, .extra.*, .contexts.trace.description, .logentry.message, .message, and .request.url/.query_string 'token=<full JWT>' - despite the docstring at :29 claiming '`?token=` is already covered by the _scrub_dict key-name denylist' (_scrub_dict is never applied to url or query_string).
findings.repro: python scratchpad/sentry_probe.py (offline, imports the real app.services.sentry_service._before_send) - prints one 'LEAKS at <json path>' line per surviving occurrence: 10 for the JWT, 4 for the admin key. SENTRY_DSN is set on the Railway `web` service, so this path is live in prod; sentry-sdk==2.68.1 (requirements.txt:142) defaults include_local_variables=True, and error_handler.py:151 calls sentry_sdk.capture_exception on every unhandled exception.
findings.impact: Any unhandled exception on an authenticated request ships the raw user JWT to a third-party SaaS inside the stack frames (get_current_user holds `token` as a local; auth_routes.py:293). Any exception inside verify_admin_key ships the PRODUCTION ADMIN_API_KEY, because both `x_admin_key` and `expected` are frame locals there - and CR-SECURITY-04 gives an unauthenticated caller a one-request way to raise exactly that exception. Request bodies (login/register payloads: email + password), cookies, and every logger.error(f'...{secret}...') that the LoggingIntegration turns into .logentry.message are likewise unscrubbed. This is not a theoretical gap: the scrubber's own docstring asserts coverage it does not have, which is why nobody re-checked.
findings.fix: Restructure _before_send to scrub the WHOLE event rather than five hand-picked keys: run _scrub_dict recursively over event['request'] (incl. data/cookies/headers), event['extra'], event['contexts'], event['user'], and event['exception']['values'][*]['stacktrace']['frames'][*]['vars'], and run _scrub_string over event['message'] and event['logentry']['message']; add 'authorization', 'bearer', 'jwt', 'key', 'expected', 'credential' to _SENSITIVE_KEY_FRAGMENTS; add a generic JWT-in-query-value rule so `?token=`/`?access_token=`/`?refresh_token=` are redacted by NAME in _scrub_query_string (the docstring's claim becomes true). Belt and braces: pass include_local_variables=False to sentry_sdk.init (sentry_service.py:215) so frames never carry locals at all - that alone kills the ADMIN_API_KEY exfil. Ships live, no flag: it only removes data from outbound events. Then delete or correct the false claim at :29-31.
findings.test_first: tests/test_sentry_scrub_coverage.py: build the fixture event from scratchpad/sentry_probe.py (JWT + admin key placed in all 12 regions), call _before_send, then walk the returned dict recursively and assert NEITHER literal appears at ANY json path. RED today with 14 hits.
findings.dedupe: new (known:M18/MB-security-01 and MB-security-02 are the MOBILE scrubber in SmartCompareApp/src/services/sentry.ts; MB-security-02 explicitly frames the backend R21 query-string scrub as the correct reference implementation the mobile side lacks. This finding shows that reference implementation is itself incomplete.)

findings.title: verify_admin_key raises TypeError on any non-ASCII X-Admin-Key: an unauthenticated request 500s all 17 admin routes and pushes the real ADMIN_API_KEY into Sentry
findings.evidence: verify_admin_key: 'if not expected or not hmac.compare_digest(x_admin_key, expected)'. Local run with ADMIN_API_KEY set: verify_admin_key('eadmin' with an acute-e) -> TypeError: comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported; verify_admin_key('<arabic kaf>') -> same. Starlette latin-1-decodes header bytes, so any 0x80-0xFF byte reaches compare_digest as a non-ASCII str.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/misc.py (offline, imports the real app.api.admin_routes.verify_admin_key). The TypeError escapes the dependency, is caught by ErrorHandlerMiddleware.dispatch (error_handler.py:138-160) which returns 500 AND calls sentry_sdk.capture_exception(exc) at :151. Per CR-SECURITY-03 the raising frame's locals - {x_admin_key, expected} - are not scrubbed, and `expected` IS the production ADMIN_API_KEY. I deliberately did NOT fire this at prod: doing so would itself exfiltrate the key into the live Sentry project.
findings.impact: One unauthenticated GET with a single high byte in X-Admin-Key turns every one of the 19 admin-key-gated routes into a 500 (availability: trivial, unmetered on the mount side) and, on the very first such request, writes the plaintext production admin key into a third-party error tracker where it persists in the event payload. The admin key is the credential for the cost dashboards, the audit log, the cohort/referral analytics and the DELETE /api/v1/text/cache flush. Two separately-benign choices (compare_digest's ASCII restriction; unscrubbed Sentry frames) compose into a credential-disclosure primitive.
findings.fix: Make the comparison byte-safe and total: encode both sides first and compare bytes - 'if not expected or not hmac.compare_digest(x_admin_key.encode("utf-8", "ignore"), expected.encode("utf-8"))' - and change the signature to 'x_admin_key: str = Header(default="")' so a MISSING header also produces the 403 path rather than a 422 (see CR-SECURITY-11). Apply the identical byte-encode to the two hmac.compare_digest sites in main.py's _AdminAuthenticatedStaticFiles (:234 header path, :244 Basic path) and to history_routes.py:148/:184. Ship together with the include_local_variables=False change from CR-SECURITY-03 so the exposure closes from both ends. No flag.
findings.test_first: tests/test_admin_key_non_ascii.py: parametrise verify_admin_key over ['é', 'ك', b'\xff'.decode('latin-1'), '', 'wrong'] and assert every one raises HTTPException(403) - never TypeError; plus a TestClient case asserting GET /api/v1/admin/costs with X-Admin-Key set to a latin-1 high byte returns 403, not 500. RED today (TypeError -> 500).

findings.title: The SSRF validator blocks the event loop on a synchronous DNS lookup - 11.07s measured for one hostile hostname, ~22s per unauthenticated /url/compare
findings.evidence: url_validator.py:30 'addr_infos = socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, None)' - a blocking C call, invoked directly from six async handlers (url_routes.py:91,112,148,175,197,216). Measured on this box: validate_external_url('https://m22-nonexistent-zzz-qqq.example/x') returned False after 11.072s; the control resolve took 0.024s. inspect: 'uses to_thread? False; uses getaddrinfo? True'.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/misc.py - times validate_external_url against a resolvable and an unresolvable host. The six call sites are inside 'async def' handlers on a single-worker uvicorn (no --proxy-headers, 1 replica), so the stall is the whole service, not one request. POST /api/v1/url/compare validates url1 AND url2 (url_routes.py:148), doubling it. An attacker controls the delay precisely by pointing the hostname at a nameserver that blackholes queries.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated caller freezes the entire deployment - every other user's compare, every /health probe, every SSE stream - for up to the resolver timeout per request, using nothing but a hostname. This is the cheapest DoS in the surface: no payload, no auth, no paid work. It compounds M18's LS-capacity-math-01 (the 10/minute limits are keyed on the shared Railway edge IP, i.e. deployment-wide), because the attacker only needs the handful of requests the limiter already lets through to hold the loop continuously. The site is in NEITHER offload set (ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD covers db_offload.run_db; ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD covers cache_service) so no existing flag mitigates it.
findings.fix: Make validate_external_url async and resolve off-loop with a hard cap: 'infos = await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.get_running_loop().getaddrinfo(hostname, None), timeout=2.0)' (loop.getaddrinfo already dispatches to the executor), treat TimeoutError as blocked, and keep a thin sync wrapper for the non-async callers in price_service/shopify_pdp/sitemap_discovery that routes through asyncio.to_thread. Await it at all six url_routes sites. Give it its own flag ENABLE_ASYNC_URL_VALIDATION (default ON is safe here - the semantics are unchanged and the only behaviour delta is that a slow resolver now fails closed at 2s instead of blocking 11s) so it can be reverted independently of the offload waves. Ordering note: unlike the limiter-key change, this needs no offload precondition.
findings.test_first: tests/test_url_validator_nonblocking.py: monkeypatch socket.getaddrinfo to sleep 3s, then run two concurrent asyncio tasks - one calling the validator, one incrementing a counter every 10ms - and assert the counter advanced during the validation (RED today: it does not). Second node: assert a resolver that never returns is abandoned within 2.5s.
findings.dedupe: new (M13's event-loop wave and M18's LS-event-loop-02/04 enumerate DB/Redis/adapter blocking sites; DNS inside the SSRF guard was never in either offload set or either finding list.)

findings.title: GET /api/v1/text/prices/{product} runs the full paid 6-region price fan-out with no auth, no usage meter and no flag gate
findings.evidence: text_routes.py:759-798: '@router.get("/prices/{product}") @limiter.limit("20/minute")' with NO auth dependency and no anon_usage_gate_enabled() block, calling 'await get_regional_prices(brand, name, variant, search_query)'. structured_comparison_service.py:8000-8007 (at 76ace90): 'for region in GCC_REGIONS.keys(): tasks.append(service._get_price(...))' then 'asyncio.gather(*tasks)'.
findings.repro: static - reading the handler and its callee at HEAD. Not fired at prod: it would spend real Serper/Scrape.do/Firecrawl/BrightData credit, which HARD RULE 1 forbids. The route's own docstring in structured_comparison_service.py:8012 already calls it 'this public endpoint (GET /text/prices/{product}) ... a SECOND response surface'.
findings.impact: Six parallel _get_price fan-outs per request - each a Serper search plus, under the prod flags ENABLE_PAGE_SCRAPE / ENABLE_SCRAPEDO / ENABLE_FIRECRAWL / ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_FALLBACK (all =true), potential paid renders - from an unauthenticated caller. Every sibling paid surface is metered or explicitly acknowledged: /text/quick and /image/identify carry the dark ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE block (text_routes.py:714, image_routes.py:87), /text/compare requires the gate too, /price-kpi is admin-gated. This one has nothing at all, and it is the highest per-request cost of them: 6 regional fan-outs versus 1. At the decorated 20/min (deployment-wide per LS-capacity-math-01) that is up to 120 paid fan-outs a minute. Not currently draining money only because the Serper balance is -50 and OpenAI is out of quota - the moment credits are topped up for the activation canaries, this is an open tap.
findings.fix: Give it the same treatment as its siblings before any credit top-up: add 'user: Optional[Dict] = Depends(get_optional_user)' plus the anon_usage_gate_enabled()/valid_device_fingerprint()/check_anon_usage_allowed() block copied from text_routes.py:714-733 and the matching record_anon_comparison fire_and_forget, and drop the limit to 5/minute. Because ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE is still dark (and blocked on #128), also add an unconditional cheap guard that this route serves cache-only when the caller is unauthenticated - i.e. pass a nocache=False/cache_only=True path into get_regional_prices - so the unmetered surface cannot originate paid work at all while the gate is off.
findings.test_first: tests/test_paid_work_gating.py, new node: patch structured_comparison_service.get_regional_prices with a mock and assert that an unauthenticated TestClient GET /api/v1/text/prices/iPhone%2015 with ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE=true and an exhausted device fingerprint returns 429 and does NOT call the mock. RED today (200, mock called). Second node mirrors the existing M13-03 pin: assert the route's dependant declares get_optional_user.
findings.dedupe: new (the known unmetered-paid-work set is /image/identify for authed users - M18/CD-interactions-06 - and the mobile lead on POST /url/compare; #63 covered /price-kpi and is closed, it now carries verify_admin_key. /text/prices was in nobody's list.)

findings.title: The comparisons RLS policy lets the anon key enumerate every shared comparison and read the share_token itself plus the owner's user_id
findings.evidence: 010:27-28 'CREATE POLICY comparisons_select ON comparisons FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id OR share_token IS NOT NULL)'. LIVE with the anon key: comparisons?share_token=not.is.null -> 0-0/1 (service_role: 0-0/1); share_token=is.null -> anon */0, service 0-0/26. select=id,user_id,share_token,query returns share_token len 22, user_id len 36.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/p5.py (SELECT-only). The 22-char value is exactly secrets.token_urlsafe(16) from database_service.py:369 - i.e. the capability secret itself is handed to the anon role, together with the row's user_id and the full 15,967-byte full_response.
findings.impact: A share token is a bearer capability: knowing it is meant to be the only way to view that comparison. This policy inverts that - anyone with the anon key lists every shared row and reads its token, so the capability model provides no confidentiality once the key is out. Worse, the direct PostgREST path bypasses the sanitisation the intended route performs: get_shared_comparison (database_service.py:410-434) strips 'personalized', 'personalization_factors', 'personalization_prompt' from full_response and never returns user_id, while the anon SELECT returns the raw row including user_id and every personalization field. Only 1 shared row exists today; the exposure scales with the referral loop, which is ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true in prod.
findings.fix: Split the policy. Keep 'comparisons_select_own' USING (auth.uid() = user_id) for the RLS-scoped user client, and remove the 'OR share_token IS NOT NULL' arm entirely - the public share path already runs through get_admin_supabase_client() (database_service.py:414) so it does not need an anon-visible policy at all. If a token-scoped anon read is genuinely wanted later, express it as a SECURITY DEFINER function that takes the token and returns the stripped payload (with an explicit REVOKE-from-PUBLIC/GRANT-to-anon pair, per CR-SECURITY-01), never as a row policy that exposes the token column. Ship in the same migration 037; the app path is unaffected because it uses the service role.
findings.test_first: In tests/test_rls_live_matrix.py (live_db): assert anon count on comparisons is 0 for every filter, including share_token=not.is.null - RED today (1). Offline companion: a source test asserting migrations/*.sql contains no policy whose USING clause references share_token.

findings.title: extract_specs_targeted has no prompt trust boundary at all: raw third-party search snippets and the raw product name go straight into the system and user messages
findings.repro: static at HEAD. Caller: structured_comparison_service.py:670 (at 76ace90) inside _fill_one_field, which builds `context` from 'search_results.get("organic")[:3]' snippets - i.e. arbitrary third-party web text - and passes brand/name/variant through unmodified. Cannot be executed end-to-end: OpenAI returns 429 insufficient_quota and the Serper balance is -50.
findings.impact: This is the one LLM call in the stack with zero injection defence. Every sibling path in extraction_service.py wraps or sanitises (sanitize_untrusted_block at :600, sanitize_prompt_input at :761-763, :1220, :1360, :1569-71, :1619-21, :1662-64) - the fix was written and never propagated to openai_service.py. A hostile snippet ranking in the top 3 for '<product> <field> specifications' can dictate the returned spec value, and a hostile product NAME lands in the SYSTEM message (a strictly higher-trust position than the <USER_INPUT> region PO-prompts-04 is about). The output is a spec field that reaches the comparison card, is persisted to comparisons.full_response, is publicly shareable via /share, and is cached 7-14 days under keys other users hit. This is a strict tightening with no flag needed, but it depends on PO-prompts-04's fix landing first - otherwise the region tag it introduces is itself escapable.

RED today - there is no tag to check.

findings.title: Logout reports success without revoking anything when Redis is unavailable - and the Supabase sign_out it also calls is a no-op on a session-less client
findings.evidence: logout_user: '_revoke_token(access_token); client = get_auth_client(); client.auth.sign_out()' then 'except Exception: logger.warning(...); return {"success": True}'. _revoke_token (:298-306) wraps the setex in try/except and only logs. get_auth_client (:26-30) does 'return create_client(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY)' - a FRESH client with no session attached.
findings.repro: static at HEAD, both branches read end-to-end. Two independent failure modes converge: (a) redis_client is None or the setex raises -> _revoke_token swallows it and the blacklist entry is never written; (b) sign_out() is called on a brand-new anon client that never had the user's session set, so it revokes nothing server-side regardless. Either way logout returns {'success': True}.
findings.impact: The user taps 'log out', the app clears local storage and shows the auth screen, and the JWT it just discarded stays fully valid for the rest of its ~1h life. On a shared or stolen device that is exactly the window that matters. verify_token's revocation check is documented fail-open (:314-319 'Fail-open if Redis unavailable'), which is a defensible availability trade-off for the CHECK - but pairing it with a WRITE that also fails silently and a route that reports success anyway means there is no path by which the system or the user learns that logout did not happen. The Supabase-side revocation, which would be the durable backstop, has never worked because of the session-less client.
findings.fix: Make _revoke_token return a bool and have logout_user propagate it: when the blacklist write fails, return 200 with {'success': True, 'revoked': False, 'code': 'REVOKE_DEGRADED'} and log at ERROR + Sentry (fire_and_forget already wraps this pattern elsewhere), so the outage is visible instead of silent. Fix the Supabase half by setting the session before signing out - 'client.auth.set_session(access_token, refresh_token)' then sign_out(scope='global') - or drop the sign_out call entirely and stop implying a server-side revocation the code does not perform. Also reconcile the blacklist TTL with the project's real JWT expiry rather than the hard-coded 3600 at :287; if Supabase's expiry is longer, revocation currently lapses early.
findings.test_first: tests/test_logout_revocation.py: (a) patch cache_service.redis_client to a stub whose setex raises, call logout_user, assert the response carries revoked=False (RED today - it returns a bare success); (b) patch redis_client to None and assert the same; (c) assert get_auth_client's returned client had set_session called before sign_out (RED today).
findings.dedupe: new (known:M18/LS-event-loop-04 covers the revocation GET being a blocking Redis call on every authed request - a performance finding on the read side. The write side silently failing while the route claims success was not filed.)

findings.title: Unauthenticated admin requests return 422 naming the x-admin-key header, re-disclosing exactly what the prod openapi/docs suppression was added to hide, and enumerating the admin route table
findings.evidence: LIVE prod, no credentials: GET /api/v1/admin/costs -> 422 {"success":false,"error":"Validation error: header - x-admin-key: Field required","code":"VALIDATION_ERROR"}. Same probe: /openapi.json 404, /docs 404. main.py:57-63 comment: 'disabling the Swagger/ReDoc UIs left the full machine-readable contract (every /admin endpoint, the X-Admin-Key header name ...) world-readable in prod'.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/prod.py - six GETs against https://web-production-58776.up.railway.app. Cause: 'def verify_admin_key(x_admin_key: str = Header(...))' makes the header a REQUIRED request parameter, so FastAPI's RequestValidationError fires before the dependency body ever runs.
findings.impact: M13-21 suppressed /openapi.json and /docs in prod specifically so the admin contract and the header name would not be world-readable; the 422 hands the header name back to any anonymous caller in one request. It also makes the admin surface enumerable without the key: a real admin path returns 422 while a non-route returns 404, so all 19 endpoints (including DELETE /api/v1/text/cache and GET /api/v1/text/parse, which share verify_admin_key) can be mapped by response code alone. Finally, 422 is semantically wrong for missing authentication - it tells monitoring 'client sent a bad request' rather than 'unauthenticated access attempt', so these never appear as auth failures in the admin_audit_log or in Sentry triage.
findings.fix: Change the dependency signature to 'x_admin_key: str = Header(default="")' so a missing header falls through to the existing check and produces the same 403 as a wrong key - missing and wrong become indistinguishable, and the route table stops being enumerable. Do this in the same edit as CR-SECURITY-04's byte-safe compare_digest, since both are one-line changes to the same function. Optionally return 401 with no detail body instead of 403 to align with the static mount's behaviour (main.py:248-253 already returns a bare 401). No flag; the only behaviour change is on unauthenticated requests.
findings.test_first: tests/test_admin_auth_shape.py: for every route whose dependant includes verify_admin_key (discovered via tests/_route_introspection.walk_routes, not a hard-coded list), assert an unauthenticated TestClient request returns 403 and that the response body contains neither 'x-admin-key' nor 'VALIDATION_ERROR'. RED today on all 19.
findings.dedupe: new (extends known:M13-21, whose fix - suppressing /openapi.json and /docs when RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT is set - is verified STILL WORKING here: both return 404 in prod. The leak simply moved to the validation error.)

findings.title: SSRF guard is TOCTOU: the validated hostname is resolved again by the fetching client with no IP pinning, and CGNAT/multicast/arbitrary ports are allowed
findings.evidence: validate_external_url resolves the hostname (:30), checks the addresses (:42), then 'return True' - it returns a boolean, never the vetted IP. Every caller then fetches by HOSTNAME (url_extraction_service.py:105 'await client.get(current, ...)'; price_service curl_cffi), so httpx/curl_cffi perform their own, second resolution. Probe: 100.64.0.1 -> True, 224.0.0.1 -> True, example.com:6379 -> True.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/ssrf_probe.py against the real validator - 20 URL forms. Good news first: 127.0.0.1, localhost, 169.254.169.254, ::1, [::ffff:127.0.0.1], [::ffff:169.254.169.254], 0.0.0.0, 2130706433, 0177.0.0.1, 0x7f.0x0.0x0.0x1, 127.1, TEST-NET and metadata.google.internal are ALL correctly blocked - the obfuscated-form hardening is real. The residue is the second resolution, plus 100.64.0.0/10 (is_private False), 224.0.0.0/4 (is_multicast, unchecked) and the absence of any port restriction.
findings.impact: An attacker who controls a nameserver returns a public A record for the validation lookup and a private one (short TTL) for the fetch - the classic DNS-rebinding bypass - and /url/extract returns the fetched page body to them, making it a full read-SSRF rather than blind. Reachability is bounded by three things that make this P2 not P1: Railway's internal network is IPv6 fd00::/8 (is_private True, so it would be caught if it were checked at connect time), redirect hops ARE re-validated at every site (url_extraction_service.py:111, price_service.py:14037, shopify_pdp_service.py:284 - the Codex hardening held), and the attack needs attacker-operated DNS. The CGNAT/multicast/port gaps are latent rather than exploited: 100.64/10 is used by some container fabrics, and nothing stops http://public-host:6379/.
findings.fix: Change the contract from 'is this URL allowed?' to 'here is the one address you may connect to': have the validator return the vetted IP (or None) and have callers connect to that IP with the original Host header - httpx supports this via a custom transport/resolver, curl_cffi via the --resolve equivalent - so the address that was checked is the address that is dialled. Fold this into the async rewrite from CR-SECURITY-05 (same function, one edit, one flag ENABLE_ASYNC_URL_VALIDATION). While in there, tighten the address predicate: add 'or ip.is_multicast or ip.is_unspecified or ip in ipaddress.ip_network("100.64.0.0/10")' and reject any explicit port outside {80, 443}.
findings.test_first: tests/test_ssrf_rebinding.py: monkeypatch socket.getaddrinfo (or the loop resolver) with a stub that returns 93.184.216.34 on the first call and 127.0.0.1 on the second, then drive the real fetch_page helper and assert it refuses to connect to 127.0.0.1 (RED today - it connects). Table-driven companion node asserting 100.64.0.1, 224.0.0.1 and https://example.com:6379/ are all rejected.
findings.dedupe: new (known:M13-20 'the Codex SSRF hardening was never propagated - adapter fetch sites follow redirects unvalidated' is a DIFFERENT gap and its status at HEAD is: mostly-fixed / partially still-open - 14 sites now use curl_fetch_html_same_site, but structured_comparison_service.py:2553 still calls the bare curl_fetch_html with allow_redirects=True on a Serper-supplied link guarded only by the substring test 'bd in link.lower()' - the same weak-hostname-match class as open issue #79. The rebinding TOCTOU is orthogonal to both and unfiled.)

findings.title: STATUS: the anon key reads the whole L2 product cache and both cohort PII views in prod - CD-db-rls-03 and CD-db-rls-04 confirmed still-open with live counts
findings.evidence: LIVE anon-key counts, identical to service_role: product_prices 3945, product_specs 643, product_reviews 627, vw_cohort_match_rate 9 (row: day, strong_matches, total_with_demographics, total_users), vw_cohort_persona_distribution 2 (row: persona='Quality-first buyer', user_count=5), bahrain_approved_drugs 655.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/rpc_probe4.py - SELECT-only, Prefer: count=exact with Range 0-0, run once with the anon key and once with the service key. Read side only: I did NOT attempt an anon INSERT/UPDATE, so the WITH CHECK (true) write half of CD-db-rls-03 remains source-only evidence.
findings.impact: Confirms two M18 findings are unfixed and quantifies them for the first time against the live database. (a) The three L2 tables that back user-served prices are fully anon-readable, and per migration 012 their policies are USING(true) + WITH CHECK(true), i.e. also anon-WRITABLE - a cache-poisoning path straight into a displayed Bahrain shelf price, which is the single thing this product cannot get wrong. product_prices carries 3,945 rows and, since 033/034 are unapplied, a poisoned row is indistinguishable from a warmed one. (b) The migration-013 cohort views have no security_invoker and no REVOKE, so aggregate demographics over the users table are readable by anon while the users table itself is correctly blocked (anon 0 / service 18) - the view launders exactly the data RLS protects. Personas over an 18-user base are effectively re-identifiable.
findings.fix: (a) Replace 012's USING(true)/WITH CHECK(true) policies with read-for-anon, write-for-service_role-only: 'CREATE POLICY l2_select ... FOR SELECT USING (true); CREATE POLICY l2_write ... FOR ALL TO service_role USING (true) WITH CHECK (true);' and REVOKE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the three tables FROM anon, authenticated. The app writes them exclusively through the service-role client, so this is behaviour-neutral. (b) Recreate the three cohort views with 'WITH (security_invoker = true)' and 'REVOKE ALL ON <view> FROM anon, authenticated; GRANT SELECT TO service_role' - the only consumer is admin_routes.py cohort_metrics/cohort_feedback/cohort_retention, all of which use the admin client. Both belong in the same migration 037 as CR-SECURITY-01/02/07 so the whole grant surface is fixed in one apply.
findings.test_first: The same tests/test_rls_live_matrix.py table used by CR-SECURITY-02, extended with the expected anon counts: product_* readable but not writable, vw_cohort_* = 0. Plus an offline source test asserting every CREATE VIEW in migrations/ carries security_invoker and is followed by a REVOKE.
findings.dedupe: known:M18/CD-db-rls-03 still-open (with fresh live evidence: 3945/643/627 rows anon-readable) and known:M18/CD-db-rls-04 still-open (fresh live evidence: both cohort views return rows to anon while the underlying users table returns none). Reported as status only, per the brief.

findings.title: The backend/ shadow application is a complete second FastAPI app with its own Procfile and railway.json and none of the security middleware
findings.evidence: backend/ holds 37 git-tracked files including app/main.py, api/{auth,text,url,routes}.py, 13 services, a Procfile ('web: uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT') and a railway.json with an identical startCommand and healthcheckPath /health. grep validate_external_url over backend/app -> 0 hits in every file. grep limiter|SecurityHeaders|ADMIN_API_KEY over backend/app/main.py -> 0 hits.

findings.impact: Dead code today - the deployed service roots at the repo top level, which is why /api/v1/admin/* and the security headers are live in prod. If someone insists on keeping it, at minimum delete backend/Procfile and backend/railway.json so it cannot be deployed by accident, and add a backend/README.md saying DEAD - NOT DEPLOYED - NO SECURITY MIDDLEWARE.

findings.title: P3 sweep: five smaller security defects across the surfaces this lane owns
findings.evidence: See per-item evidence below; all read at HEAD 76ace90.
findings.repro: static reads plus the two scratchpad probes already cited (envscan.py, route_table.py).
findings.impact: (1) UNBOUNDED URL STRINGS - url_routes.py:29/34-36 declare 'url: str', 'url1: str', 'url2: str' with no max_length, and the GET variants use Query(...) with no constraint (url_routes.py:107, 168-170). Every sibling text route pins its input (text_routes prices/{product} uses Path(max_length=100), variant Query(max_length=50); history search Query(max_length=100)). A multi-megabyte string is accepted, urlparse'd and logged at INFO (url_routes.py:88 'logger.info(f"URL extraction request: {body.url}")') on the single worker. FIX: Field(max_length=2048) on all three plus max_length on the Query params, and truncate the log line. (2) IMAGE SIZE CHECK RUNS AFTER THE READ - image_routes.py:113-119 does 'content = await img.read()' and only then compares len(content) to 10MB, four times; the 10MB cap never limits what is buffered/spooled first. FIX: stream-and-count, or read in chunks and abort past the cap. (3) M13-29 STILL PARTIALLY OPEN - comparison_id is now UUID-format-validated at the Pydantic layer (feedback_routes.py:26, :117 - the format half of the M13-29 fix landed) but ownership is still never checked and the write still goes through the service-role client, so an anonymous caller can still pin 50 events per request at 60/min onto any comparison_id. Materially easier now that CR-SECURITY-02 hands out comparison_ids. dedupe known:M13-29 still-open. FIX: verify the comparison belongs to the caller (or drop the field for anonymous callers). (4) INCONSISTENT OWNERSHIP COMPARISON - history_routes.py:148 and :184 use hmac.compare_digest for the ownership check while database_service.py:359 (create_share_token) uses a plain '!='; neither is a secret comparison so both are functionally fine, but the inconsistency invites the wrong conclusion in review, and compare_digest on a str is the same non-ASCII TypeError trap as CR-SECURITY-04. FIX: pick one - plain == on UUIDs - and comment why. (5) TWENTY UNMETERED ROUTES CONFIRMED - the decorator census shows 20 routes carry no @limiter.limit (auth logout/me/verify/profile-PUT/preferences-GET/preferences-PUT/cohort-profile, legal x4, referrals/status, text/cache, text/parse, url/retailers, usage/status, app/version, /, /favicon.ico, /health) and ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS is absent from the Railway `web` variable list, so rate_limiter.py:89 reads '' and main.py:135 never adds SlowAPIMiddleware - the blanket default_limits are inert in prod. dedupe known:M18/LS-ratelimit-02 still-open, and correctly held behind #114's ordering rule (the mis-keyed limiter currently protects the loop).
findings.fix: Items 1, 2 and 4 are small independent edits with no flag. Item 3 needs the ownership check plus a decision about anonymous feedback, and should be sequenced after CR-SECURITY-02 closes (otherwise comparison_ids stay freely harvestable). Item 5 is a status confirmation only - do NOT act on it before the offload waves are active, per the M18 ordering rule that the mis-keyed limiter is currently the thing protecting the single event loop.

findings.title: ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM puts the 1.0 presence credit on the same numeric axis as real magnitudes, so an unparseable spec value is scored as the number 1 and can beat (or be beaten by) a measured one
findings.evidence: _score_specs_fields at :1855-1866: `if numeric is not None and field in higher: field_values[field]=numeric / elif ... in lower: -numeric / else: field_values[field] = 1.0  # presence credit (legacy `+= 1`)`. _apply_spec_field_normalization then pair-min-maxes those raw values together (:1925-1943). In the LEGACY _score_specs the presence credit 1.0 was summed with already-normalized ratios, so 1.0 meant 'best'; here it is literally the number one on a magnitude axis. The 10x unit-mismatch guard at :1934-1938 only fires when the ratio reaches 10, so anything inside 10x is scored as a genuine advantage.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/m22-review/r2.py against tree76 (real ScoringService). Case A (fragrances, longevity is HIGHER_IS_BETTER): 'longevity: 8 hours' -> 8.0 vs 'longevity: Long lasting' -> presence 1.0 gives ratios {longevity: 0.932} vs {longevity: 0.068} and flips character_score 73.0 vs 57.0. Case A2 (electronics, weight is LOWER_IS_BETTER so magnitudes are NEGATED): 'weight: 1.5 kg' -> -1.5 vs 'weight: Lightweight' -> +1.0; min/max = (-1.5, 1.0), 1.5/1.0 < 10 so the guard does not fire, ratios come out {weight: 0.0} vs {weight: 1.0} and spec_raw 0.2576 vs 0.5152 -- the product with NO parseable weight wins the weight field outright and the whole spec dimension.
findings.impact: Dark flag (ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM default OFF, unset in Railway), so at most P2 today. But this is issue #100's headline fix and the whole point is a fairer spec score: on flip, every schema field where one side's value is prose and the other's is numeric within 10x becomes a fabricated 1.0-vs-0.0 advantage, and on any LOWER_IS_BETTER field (electronics weight, grocery nutrition_calories/carbs/fat, supplements nutrition_calories) the sign flip means the side with UNPARSEABLE data systematically wins. LLM-extracted specs routinely mix prose and numerals ('All-day', 'Long lasting', 'Lightweight'), so this is a common shape, not a corner.
findings.fix: Do not let presence credit share the magnitude axis. In _score_specs_fields return the presence-credit fields in a SEPARATE map (e.g. a third element, or a sentinel like None) and in _apply_spec_field_normalization score them structurally: a field where BOTH sides are presence-only ties at 0.5, a field where one side is numeric and the other presence-only is a NON-COMPARABLE basis and must tie at 0.5 (the same treatment the >=10x unit-mismatch guard already gives), and only a field where BOTH sides parsed to numbers goes through _magnitude_aware_ratio. That also removes the sign hazard, because the mixed case never reaches the min/max. Keep it behind ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM.
findings.test_first: New tests/test_scoring_spec_field_normalization.py case, red today: with monkeypatch.setenv('ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM','true'), two electronics products identical except weight='1.5 kg' vs weight='Lightweight'; call ScoringService()._compute_raw_scores on each then _apply_spec_field_normalization and assert the ratios for 'weight' are equal (0.5, 0.5) -- i.e. an unparseable value never wins a lower-is-better field. Second case: fragrances longevity '8 hours' vs 'Long lasting' must also tie at 0.5.

findings.title: #102's honest-absence branch is dead code: breakdown never carries None, so a product with a fully unavailable price still ships value_badge 'fair_price' -- and the only test pinning it uses a shape the runtime never produces
findings.evidence: apply_value_badges:2520-2526: `value_score = breakdown.get(value_dim); if value_score is None: continue`. The docstring at :2504-2511 promises 'When the value dim is genuinely absent, NO badge is set -- an absent badge is honest, a defaulted one is a claim.' But `breakdown` is built in _normalize_scores:2214-2233 as `scores[dim] = signal_arrays[signal][i]`, and value_scores comes from _compute_value_score, which returns MISSING_SCORE (50.0), never None. The ENABLE_BUNDLE_C_SCORING None-propagation at :1751-1753 writes into raw_scores, NOT into the normalized breakdown the badge reads. Pinning test tests/test_value_badge_category_dims.py:203-222 (test_absent_value_dim_emits_no_badge) hand-builds `"product_0": {"breakdown": {"character_score": 80.0}}` with wear_value_score OMITTED -- compute_scores always emits every dim in CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS[category], so that dict shape cannot occur.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/m22-review/r2.py, block D, against tree76: two fragrance products, product_0 with price {amount: None, unavailable: True} and empty specs, ENABLE_CATEGORY_VALUE_BADGE=true, run svc.compute_scores then svc.apply_value_badges. Output (scratchpad/m22-review/r2.txt): `D bundleC=false badges: ['fair_price','fair_price'] value dim: wear_value_score breakdown: [50, 68.0]` and `D bundleC=true badges: ['fair_price','fair_price'] ... breakdown: [50, 68.0]`. findings.impact: Dark flag today (ENABLE_CATEGORY_VALUE_BADGE unset in Railway) so P2, but on flip the fix ships only its first half. A product whose price is entirely unavailable -- exactly the pending-price shape the region-currency guard and the pending-price chokepoint produce -- still gets a positive 'fair_price' badge computed from the injected 50 sentinel and a defaulted 'mid' tier. findings.fix: Read missingness from the authoritative source rather than value identity, exactly the way _missing_dim_renorm_enabled does: have compute_scores expose per-product missing dims (it already emits `missing_data` at :1433 and, under renorm, `excluded_dims`) and make apply_value_badges skip the badge when value_dim is in that product's `missing_data` list, in addition to the existing `is None` guard. That is a pure read of an already-shipped key and needs no new plumbing. Keep it inside the ENABLE_CATEGORY_VALUE_BADGE branch.
findings.test_first: Rewrite tests/test_value_badge_category_dims.py::test_absent_value_dim_emits_no_badge to build its scoring_result by CALLING ScoringService().compute_scores on two fragrance products where product_0 has price {'amount': None, 'unavailable': True} and specs {} -- not from a hand-written dict -- then assert 'value_badge' not in products[0]. It is red today (ships 'fair_price') and it is the only version of the test that can catch this class of defect.

findings.title: ENABLE_CITATION_RUBRIC_V2 downgrades correctly-cited numeric specs to 'unverified' whenever the snippet hyphenates the unit ('6.1-inch'), because the snippet regex only allows whitespace between number and unit
findings.evidence: _SNIPPET_NUM_UNIT_RE at fcs:128-130 is `(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(<units>|\")(?![a-z0-9])` -- `\s*` matches spaces and nothing else, so 'a 6.1-inch display' yields NO (number, unit) pair on the snippet side. _grade_citation_v2:170-186 then finds same_unit empty, sets all_matched False with contradicted False, and returns 'unverified'. The LEGACY rubric (still at fcs:235-255 under the flag-OFF branch) fell through to term overlap for 'inch' and returned 'verified'.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/m22-review/r1.py against tree76 (calls the real fact_check_service.verify_spec_citations). Snippet 'The iPhone has a 6.1-inch display, 128 GB storage and a 5000mAh battery.' with specs display='6.1 inch'/storage='128 GB'/battery='5000 mAh': OFF -> {display: verified, storage: verified, battery: verified}; ON -> {display: UNVERIFIED, storage: verified, battery: verified}. Same snippet re-spelled '6.1 inch' -> ON returns verified, proving the hyphen is the sole cause. Prevalence measured offline over the 1,655-file _proof corpus (zero network): 47,505 hyphenated number+unit spellings vs 63,256 spaced -- ~43% of all number+unit occurrences use a hyphen.
findings.impact: Dark flag (ENABLE_CITATION_RUBRIC_V2 unset) so P2. On flip it is a systematic false negative on the most common consumer-electronics spec spelling. Because #109's ACTIVATION ORDER puts CITATION_RUBRIC_V2 upstream of the confidence wiring, every such field drops out of both verified_pct and citation_count (which #109 redefines as verified+likely at scoring_service:1020), pulling the specs confidence pill down on exactly the comparisons the citation layer was supposed to make MORE trustworthy -- and _score_reliability reads the same counts, so the reliability dimension moves too. It would be attributed to the flag as 'the model cites badly' rather than to a regex.
findings.fix: Allow the standard hyphen family between number and unit in the SNIPPET pattern (the value side too, harmlessly): change `\s*` to `[\s‐-―-]*` in both _VALUE_NUM_UNIT_RE and _SNIPPET_NUM_UNIT_RE, or normalize the snippet/value with a pre-pass that collapses `(\d)[‐-―-](?=[a-z\"])` to `\1 ` before matching, mirroring _strip_thousands_separators. Keep the whole thing inside ENABLE_CITATION_RUBRIC_V2 and re-run the flag-OFF golden. Note the same `\s*` appears in _shopping_number_confirmed's adjacency probe at fcs:295-298 and needs the identical fix or the shopping identity fence inherits the bug.
findings.test_first: New case in tests/test_fact_checking.py, red today: monkeypatch.setenv('ENABLE_CITATION_RUBRIC_V2','true'); verify_spec_citations({'display':'6.1 inch','display_source':'snippet_1'}, ['a 6.1-inch OLED display']) must == {'display':'verified'}. Add the mirror for '128-GB' and '5,000-mAh', and one negative control asserting '6.1-inch' vs a snippet saying '6.7-inch' still returns 'flagged'.

findings.title: #116 lengthened the savings cache TTL 5min -> 6h unflagged, and both branches still cache the DEGRADED zero payload, so one Supabase blip hides a user's savings banner for six hours
findings.evidence: home_routes.py:120 `_SAVINGS_TTL_SECONDS = 6 * 60 * 60`, up from `5 * 60`, unflagged (the aggregate itself is behind ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE but the TTL is not). Flag-OFF path :257-261: `except Exception as exc: logger.error(...); rows = []` then FALLS THROUGH to build `payload = {savings_bhd: 0.0, decisions_count: 0, threshold_met: False}` and :283-286 writes it with ex=_SAVINGS_TTL_SECONDS. Flag-ON path :226-242 does the same with `total_savings, decisions_count = 0.0, 0`. The bust-on-write contract (:112-118) has exactly two writers -- history_routes.py:210 and feedback_service.py:59, both `delete_cached(f"home:savings:{user_id}")` -- and both fire only when the user saves or deletes a comparison.
findings.repro: Static, read at HEAD in scratchpad/m22-review/tree76/app/api/home_routes.py:203-288 and cross-checked against every writer (grep 'home:savings' over app/ returns exactly home_routes:204, history_routes:210, feedback_service:59; grep 'table(\"comparisons\")' plus the save_comparison_and_track_cohort call graph confirms all 4 comparison writers -- text POST:278, text GET:427, text stream:648, image:265 -- go through the busting helper). Not reproduced against live Redis: BRIEF rule 1 forbids writing to prod Redis.
findings.impact: Live today on the shipped flag set. A user who opens Home during any transient Supabase failure (or a token-scoped RLS denial) gets savings_bhd 0 / threshold_met false cached for SIX HOURS; the FE hides the SavingsBanner on threshold_met=false, and the only thing that clears it is the user running or deleting a comparison. Before #116 the same failure self-healed in 5 minutes. The blast radius of a degraded read was multiplied 72x by a change whose stated rationale was purely about recompute cost. It also compounds with the flag-ON path: flipping ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE before migration 036 is applied (it is written but UNAPPLIED, like 033/034/035) makes the RPC 404 (PGRST202) on every call, and each 404 pins a zero banner for 6h per user.
findings.fix: Never cache a degraded result. In both branches, track whether the read actually succeeded and skip the _redis_set_async when it did not (or write it with a short 60s negative TTL), returning the empty payload uncached. Concretely: hoist a `degraded = False` flag, set it in each except, and guard the cache write with `if not degraded`. Keep the 6h TTL for successful reads -- the bust-on-write contract genuinely covers those. Unflagged, since it only narrows what gets persisted.
findings.test_first: tests/test_home_routes.py, red today: patch home_routes.run_db (or the client) to raise, patch home_routes._redis_set to a recording double, call GET /api/v1/home/savings, assert the response is the empty payload AND that _redis_set was NOT called with home:savings:{uid} (or was called with ex<=60). Add the twin for the flag-ON branch with _fetch_savings_aggregate raising.

findings.title: ENABLE_COMPARISON_QUALITY_V2 relabels sparse data 'weird'->'weak', which silently TURNS ON the client's winner-reveal celebration for the thin-evidence comparisons that previously suppressed it
findings.evidence: scs:858 and scs:909 `_sparse_label = "weak" if comparison_quality_v2_enabled() else "weird"`. The same signal reaches the payload unconditionally: response_builder.py:348-349 `_safe_detect_comparison_quality` -> `detect_comparison_quality(product_data, post_fallback=True)`, emitted at response_builder:1185 and :1859 as scoring_v2.comparison_quality. The shipped client gates on the exact string: SmartCompareApp/src/components/results/ResultsContent.tsx:425 `const isWeird = scoring_v2.comparison_quality === 'weird';` and :434 `{!isWeird && winnerRevealed ? (<RevealBurst .../>) : null}`. 'weak' is a declared member of ComparisonQuality (types.ts:423) but nothing branches on it, so it falls through the gate as if it were 'normal'.
findings.repro: Static trace through both trees, cross-checked at HEAD in tree76. Cannot be driven end-to-end: OpenAI is dead (429 insufficient_quota) so no live compare is possible. The flip is deterministic and gated on a string equality, so no runtime is needed to establish it. Prevalence is taken from the M18 measurement quoted in the flag's own docstring at scs:816-822 -- 'weird' was the modal label on real traffic, 14 of 15 recorded rows, purely from thin early-pipeline data.
findings.impact: Dark flag today (ENABLE_COMPARISON_QUALITY_V2 unset in Railway) so P2, and the phones run the 97b5f15 preview bundle which contains this same gate. On flip, ~93% of comparisons (14/15 recorded) move from a suppressed results card to a celebratory emerald RevealBurst -- the app would start celebrating a winner precisely on the comparisons where the backend has simultaneously started telling the verdict model to HEDGE (_WEAK_VERDICT_INSTRUCTION, extraction_service:2020). The prose says 'based on the available data' while the UI throws confetti. Nothing in the flag's design notes, the M18 rows, or the mobile checkup covers this cross-tier interaction, and a canary would read the celebration-rate jump as an engagement win.
findings.fix: Make the client gate on the CONFIDENCE of the signal, not on one literal. Change ResultsContent.tsx:425 to `const isLowQuality = scoring_v2.comparison_quality !== 'normal';` and use that for the RevealBurst gate (an allowlist on 'normal' rather than a denylist on 'weird'), so any future member of ComparisonQuality is fail-closed. Ship that in the SAME OTA as, or before, the ENABLE_COMPARISON_QUALITY_V2 flip -- the two-lever gap means the backend flag can be flipped from Railway in seconds while the client fix needs an `eas update --branch preview`, so the ordering is a hard precondition, not a preference.
findings.test_first: SmartCompareApp jest, red today: render ResultsContent with scoring_v2.comparison_quality='weak', winnerRevealed=true and >=3 dimensions, and assert queryByTestId('results-v2-reveal-burst-slot') is null. Back it with a backend test asserting detect_comparison_quality(sparse_pair, post_fallback=True) == 'weak' under the flag, so the pair is pinned on both sides of the wire.

findings.title: P3 sweep: seven latent defects in the M20/M21 delta
findings.evidence: (a) scoring_service.py:1554-1557 -- compute_scores still builds its INTERNAL product_names with the raw `f"{brand} {name}".strip()` concat for dimension_winners and price_tiers, while :913 (_product_name_for_evidence) and scs:1077 (_display_product_names) now route through dedup_brand_name. Same result dict therefore carries 'TOM FORD TOM FORD OUD WOOD' in dimension_winners/price_tiers and the deduped spelling in winner_evidence. dimension_winners is typed in SmartCompareApp/src/types/types.ts:253 but never rendered, so it is persisted-inconsistency only. (b) app/api/text_routes.py:247,400,673,687 and the anon twin -- consume_comparison_credit/check_anon_usage_allowed now RETURN `consumed_keys` (usage_service.py:390-393, :138-142) and refund_comparison_credit ACCEPTS it (:absent second arg), but not one of the 5 refund call sites passes it, so the entire deterministic-symmetry half of the M18 usage-symmetry fix is dead wiring and every refund falls back to the current+previous-window heuristic. (c) response_builder.py:1280 and :1289 -- _strip_inference_markers deletes any dict ENTRY and any list ITEM whose VALUE is the bare string 'model_knowledge', not just keys containing 'inference_source'; a legitimate field or list element equal to that string is silently removed from the response AND from the persisted full_response. (d) scoring_service.py:1945 -- _apply_spec_field_normalization applies `mean * (0.5 + coverage_ratio)` UNCONDITIONALLY, while legacy _score_specs:1819-1823 applies its penalty only when coverage_ratio < CATEGORY_MIN_COVERAGE; under ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM a fully-covered product's spec_raw can reach 1.5, silently changing the coverage rule for well-covered products as well as sparse ones. (e) fact_check_service.py:523 -- `bhd_rate = _convert_to_bhd(1.0, target)` has NO unconvertible-code guard, although the row-side currency two lines earlier (:515) does exactly that check; _convert_to_bhd returns the amount UNCHANGED for a code outside the effective table, so a BHD-based median would be compared against a non-BHD final amount. Latent only: REGION_TO_CURRENCY is {BHD,SAR,AED,KWD,QAR,OMR} and all six are in the 13-code base FALLBACK_RATES (verified by executing exchange_rate_service in tree76). (f) response_builder.py:157-163 -- deterministic_verdict_fields resolves the loser with `1 - winner_index`, valid only for exactly two products; a 3-product result would look up 'product_-1' and silently degrade the reason text. (g) migrations/036_home_savings_aggregate.sql:70 -- the SQL accepts winner_index JSON strings '0'/'1' (documented) but the Python at home_routes.py:163 `winner_idx not in (0, 1)` ALSO accepts JSON `true` as index 1, because `True == 1` in Python; the SQL rejects it. findings.title: extract_domain uses a SUBSTRING www replace and never lowercases — 'shopwww.example.com' becomes 'shopexample.com' and it is byte-duplicated in review_service (MEASURED)
findings.evidence: price_service.py:3177-3184 `domain = parsed.netloc.replace("www.", "")` — a str.replace, not a prefix strip, and no .lower(). review_service.py:135-142 is byte-identical (AST identical-body pass, work/dupes.txt group 6). Ran the real function at 76ace90: extract_domain('https://shopwww.example.com/p') -> 'shopexample.com'; ('https://WWW.Nahdionline.COM/p') -> 'WWW.Nahdionline.COM'; ('https://nahdionline.com:443/p') -> 'nahdionline.com:443'; ('https://www.wwwtech.com/p') -> 'wwwtech.com' (correct by luck). Contrast source_router._normalize_domain, which DOES lowercase.
findings.repro: MEASURED, local off-lock: python scratchpad/m22-review/work/repro_www.out generator — imports app.services.price_service from the 76ace90 tree and calls ps.extract_domain on the five URLs above. Also repro_host.py which runs 9 host normalisers side by side.
findings.impact: Two live consumers. (1) price_service.py:9664-9666 inside `extract_price_from_shopping`: `domain = extract_domain(link); if domain in OFFICIAL_BRAND_DOMAINS: retailer_score = 1.0` — a corrupted or upper-cased host silently misses the official-brand set, so a first-party listing loses its 1.0 score and can be out-ranked by a reseller in the Serper-shopping tier. (2) review_service.py:306-312: the same corrupted string is written straight into `quote["retailer"]`, i.e. a USER-VISIBLE attribution label on a review quote. Probability is low per request (needs 'www' inside a label, upper-case, or an explicit port) but the failure is silent and there is no test on either behaviour. The duplication means fixing one copy leaves the other wrong — exactly the M13 'fixed-once-never-propagated' pattern.
findings.fix: Replace both bodies with one shared helper — put it in app/utils/ (not price_service, to avoid adding to the 15,940-LOC file) as `registrable_host(url)` implemented like `_not_a_pdp_registrable_domain` (price_service.py:12262): urlsplit, take .hostname (which drops userinfo and port and lowercases), strip a leading 'www.' by prefix not substring, return ''. Point price_service.extract_domain and review_service._extract_domain at it, keep the old names as one-line aliases so the 3 call sites and the structured_comparison_service shim at :2688 are untouched. Behaviour changes only for the corrupt inputs, so ship it plain — but pin the OFFICIAL_BRAND_DOMAINS lookup with a test first because it changes retailer_score for upper-cased hosts.

findings.title: Nine host-normalisation implementations across eight services return up to four different answers for the same URL
findings.evidence: Ran all nine at 76ace90 on 'HTTPS://WWW.Nahdionline.COM/p': price_service.extract_domain:3177 and review_service._extract_domain:135 -> 'WWW.Nahdionline.COM'; occ_service._normalize_domain:86, rest_json_service._normalize_domain:90, firecrawl_service._normalize_host:272, sitemap_discovery._bare_host:299 -> 'nahdionline.com'; shopify_pdp_service._normalise_domain:146 and sitemap_discovery._norm_domain:191 -> 'https://www.nahdionline.com/p' (they do not parse the URL at all — they return the input unless it is already bare). On '//nahdionline.com/p' the answers split three ways: 'nahdionline.com' / '//nahdionline.com/p' / ''. Full matrix in work/repro_host.out; the cluster census (work/dupes.txt) counts 31 host/registry functions across 12 modules.
findings.repro: MEASURED, local off-lock: python scratchpad/m22-review/work/repro_host.py — imports the eight real service modules from the 76ace90 tree, calls each normaliser on 10 constructed URLs, prints the per-case distinct-answer partition.
findings.impact: Every adapter decides for itself what a host is, so a registry row that matches in source_router can fail to match in shopify_pdp_service and vice versa. This is the mechanism behind the standing host-matching issues (#79 pharmacy hostname match, #94 registry wrong 4 rows, #76 wire virginmegastore/Alshaya): a fix applied to one normaliser cannot propagate. `shopify_pdp_service._normalise_domain` and `sitemap_discovery._norm_domain` are the dangerous pair — they pass a full URL through unchanged, so any `if _normalise_domain(x) in REGISTRY` they feed is a guaranteed miss for URL-shaped input.
findings.fix: Introduce one `app/utils/hosts.py` with `registrable_host(value)` (urlsplit -> .hostname -> lower -> strip leading 'www.' -> public-suffix-aware two/three-label reduction reusing _NOT_A_PDP_TWO_LEVEL_SUFFIXES) and one `bare_host(value)` for the sub-domain-preserving case. Migrate one module per commit, starting with the two that do not parse at all (shopify_pdp_service:146, sitemap_discovery:191) since those are the ones whose current output cannot match any registry key; keep each old name as an alias so call sites are untouched. Do this BEFORE #79/#94, otherwise those fixes land in one normaliser only.

findings.title: build_comparison_response takes 22 keyword parameters with two aliased for the same value, and one of its three call sites silently omits verdict_validation
findings.evidence: response_builder.py:1295-1318 declares 22 keyword-only params (711 LOC body, cc=122 — the third-highest in the backend). `product_data` and `products` are documented aliases for the same argument ('Pass either; if both are passed products wins'). AST diff of the three call sites in structured_comparison_service.py: L3557 and L4308 pass 21 kwargs each; L3000 passes 20 — it omits `verdict_validation`. response_builder.py:1362 turns the missing value into `{}` and :1854 emits it as `response["verdict_validation"]`. The producer `validate_verdict` is called only at structured_comparison_service.py:3483 and :4209, both on streaming paths — the non-streaming `_compare_from_text_impl` never runs trust validation at all.
findings.repro: static: python - to AST-walk structured_comparison_service.py for Call nodes named build_comparison_response and diff their keyword sets -> work/bcr.out. Then grep -n 'verdict_validation' app/services/structured_comparison_service.py app/services/response_builder.py.
findings.impact: A 22-parameter constructor is an interface where forgetting an argument is silent and typed as valid. It already happened: `GET /api/v1/text/compare` (non-streaming) always returns `verdict_validation: {}` while the SSE path returns the real trust-validation dict. Nothing consumes the field today — `grep -rn verdict_validation SmartCompareApp/src` is empty — so there is no user harm now, which is why it is P2 and not P1; but the same shape means any future field added to the streaming path defaults silently on the JSON path, and the two endpoints are supposed to be response-compatible. cc=122 over 711 LOC also makes the assembly untestable except through the whole pipeline.
findings.fix: Collapse the 22 params into 3-4 dataclasses that mirror how the values are actually produced — `ComparisonInputs(product_data, product_names, comparison, scoring_result, tradeoffs, confidence, verdict_validation)`, `RequestContext(query, region, category_used, category_switched, original_category, user_preferences, cohort_summary, from_cache)`, `CostMeters(total_cost, api_calls, gpt_calls, serper_calls, elapsed_seconds)` — so a missing field is a constructor error, not a default. Drop the `products`/`product_data` alias (one caller, one name). Separately and first: decide whether the non-streaming path should run validate_verdict; if yes, call it in `_compare_from_text_impl` before L3000 and pass it — that is a response-shape change, so ship it behind the existing ENABLE_CONFIDENCE_FACTCHECK_WIRING-style pattern with a new dark flag if the mobile client is ever taught to read the field.
findings.test_first: tests/test_response_contract_parity.py::test_streaming_and_json_responses_have_the_same_keys — build both responses from the same recorded fixture (tests/fixtures/comparison_baseline_d2*.json) and assert set(json_response) == set(stream_final_response) and that verdict_validation is non-empty in both. RED today on verdict_validation.

findings.title: Nine mutually-dependent service pairs are held apart only by 98 function-local imports in the two god modules — 20 import cycles exist below module level
findings.evidence: Full AST import graph over 105 app/ modules: 0 module-level cycles, but 20 cycles once function-local imports are included, and 9 mutual pairs — cache_service<->price_service, extraction_service<->review_service, extraction_service<->price_service, magento_graphql_service<->price_service, price_service<->shopify_pdp_service, price_service<->sitemap_discovery_service, price_service<->salla_service, response_builder<->structured_comparison_service, search_descriptor_service<->source_router. Deferred-import counts: price_service.py 50, structured_comparison_service.py 48 (work/godmodules.txt). Concrete edges: cache_service.py:425 `from app.services.price_service import (` inside a function; extraction_service.py:1171, :2283, :2567 the same.
findings.repro: static: python scratchpad/m22-review/work/an8.py — builds two graphs (module-level edges vs all edges) over app/ and reports DFS back-edges -> work/cycles.txt.
findings.impact: Every one of those 98 in-function imports is load-bearing: hoisting any of them to module scope is an immediate ImportError at startup, so the dependency structure is unfixable by refactoring one file. It also means the true module graph is invisible to any tool that reads only module-level imports (including the reachability analysis in this lane, which I had to widen). Runtime cost is small but non-zero on the single event loop — each call re-enters the import machinery and takes the module lock. Practically, it is why price_service.py cannot be split: it is transitively coupled to cache, extraction, shopify, salla, magento and sitemap in both directions.
findings.fix: Break the pairs by direction, one commit each, cheapest first. The three adapter pairs (salla, magento, shopify_pdp) are the easy ones: they import price_service only for parse/format helpers (parse_money, is_price_showable, currency labels) — move those helpers to a new leaf module app/services/price_primitives.py that neither side imports back, then both sides import the leaf at module level and the cycle is gone. Do the same for cache_service<->price_service (cache_service.py:425 needs price predicates) and response_builder<->structured_comparison_service. Leave extraction_service<->review_service last; it is a genuine two-way collaboration and wants a seam, not a helper move. Add the leaf-module rule to CLAUDE.md so new adapters do not recreate the cycle.
findings.test_first: tests/test_no_import_cycles.py::test_app_services_have_no_cycles_even_via_deferred_imports — AST-build the full edge set (module-level plus function-local) over app/ and assert the graph is a DAG. RED with 20 cycles today; it can be ratcheted (assert len(cycles) <= N, lowering N per commit).
