findings.title: extract_price_from_html parses the SAME html with BeautifulSoup four times per call — measured 40 soups for 10 pages, 3 of every 4 pure waste
findings.evidence: `extract_jsonld_price` starts with `soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')` (price_service.py:10642) and `extract_price_from_html` calls it THREE times on the same string — 13092 (target currency), 13097 (USD retry), 13112 (accept_any_currency, gated on `jsonld_first_enabled()` whose docstring says "default ON") — then builds its OWN soup at 13056. Harness `m_soup.py` counted BeautifulSoup.__init__ per call over 10 cached `_proof/html/*.html` PDPs: soups=4 on every single page, 40 total, 17,110,052 bytes parsed for 4,351,425 bytes of input (3.93x). cProfile: `bs4.__init__:211` cumtime 4.286 s of extract_price_from_html's 4.839 s = 88.6%; `extract_jsonld_price` ncalls=30 for 10 outer calls.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/perf/m_soup.py out.json  (zero network; reads 10 pages >20 KB from _proof/html). Also: python scratchpad/perf/prof_extract.py out.txt for the cProfile.
findings.impact: MEASURED 2549 ms of pure blocking CPU for 10 pages (93–550 ms/page, median 217 ms) on the dev box; ~75% of that (≈1.9 s / ≈190 ms per page) is the three duplicate parses. `fetch_page_price` calls it INLINE inside `async def` (price_service.py:14090, after `await curl_fetch_html_same_site`), and so do `_firecrawl_scraper` (scs:1643) and `_scrapedo_scraper` (scs:1722) — so this is CPU on the single uvicorn event loop, not in a thread. ENABLE_PAGE_SCRAPE=true in prod. Every Tier-1.5 HTML candidate pays it; N candidate pages = N x ~190 ms of avoidable loop stall inside a 15 s price race and a 30 s STREAM_HARD_CAP, which is exactly the budget the 1288 'Still gathering prices' + 209 'couldn't finish in time' rows in search_logs are losing.
findings.fix: Parse once and thread the soup through. Give `extract_jsonld_price` an optional `soup=` parameter (default None -> parse, so no call site outside this file changes) and have `extract_price_from_html` build its single soup BEFORE the JSON-LD ladder and pass it into all three calls. The three passes differ only in `expected_currency`/`accept_any_currency`, never in markup, so this is byte-identical by construction; if a flag is wanted, gate on ENABLE_SHARED_SOUP_PARSE and keep the None default as the legacy path. Do this before, and independently of, the parser swap in CR-PERFORMANCE-02.
findings.test_first: tests/test_price_extract_soup_reuse.py: monkeypatch `bs4.BeautifulSoup.__init__` with a counter, call `extract_price_from_html(html, 'X', 'BHD', 'd.com', 'https://d.com/p')` on a fixture page whose JSON-LD has no matching offer (so all three ladder passes run), assert the counter == 1. RED today (== 4).

findings.title: Every Serper/rating/image call builds and discards a fresh httpx.AsyncClient — 21–26 per compare, and each rebuilds the certifi SSL context on the event loop (measured 45–52% of compare wall)
findings.evidence: `async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=_serper_timeout()) as client:` at serper_service.py:649 (also :776, :985, :1118, rating_service.py:279). Harness `drive_compare.py` with a stack-capturing counter: COLD compare = 26 `httpx.AsyncClient.__init__` and 26 `ssl.SSLContext.load_verify_locations`, 17 of them from serper_service.py:649; WARM = 21 and 21, 15 from :649. Accumulated timer inside `load_verify_locations`: COLD 6541.7 ms of a 12672.3 ms compare (51.6%); WARM 4947.0 ms of 10954.7 ms (45.2%). Isolated (`m_ssl.py`): `httpx.AsyncClient()` = 365 ms p50, `ssl.load_verify_locations(certifi 270,954 B)` = 243 ms p50.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/perf/drive_compare.py out.json cold  (prints `TIMERS {'ssl.load_verify_locations_ms': ...}` per run). python scratchpad/perf/m_ssl.py out.json for the isolated ctor cost.
findings.impact: #73 framed this as a lost TCP+TLS handshake (network). The measurement says the DOMINANT term is CPU that runs BEFORE any socket opens: parsing the 271 KB CA bundle into a fresh SSLContext, synchronously, on the single event loop, 21–26 times per compare. Keep-alive alone would not fix it. Dev-box ms are Windows/off-lock and Railway/Linux is UNMEASURED (my 4-sample prod probe was swamped by 0.7–2.7 s client RTT), but the COUNT is platform-independent and every one of those builds is head-of-line blocking for every other concurrent request on the 1-worker uvicorn.
findings.fix: Two changes, both small. (1) Build ONE module-level `ssl.SSLContext` (or one `httpx.Limits`+`verify=` context) at import and pass `verify=_SHARED_SSL_CTX` at all 20 construction sites listed in #73 — this alone removes the CPU term with zero behavioural change. (2) Then replace the per-call `async with httpx.AsyncClient(...)` with a lazily-created module-level pooled client per vendor host, closed on FastAPI shutdown, to recover keep-alive. Ship (1) unflagged (it cannot change a response) and (2) behind ENABLE_POOLED_HTTPX_CLIENTS.
findings.test_first: tests/test_httpx_client_pooling.py: patch `ssl.SSLContext.load_verify_locations` with a counter, run `await search_web('x')` twice with `_serper_post` stubbed, assert the counter did not increase on the second call. RED today (+1 per call).
findings.dedupe: known:#73 — still-open. #73 lists the sites and estimates '~10-16 Serper calls' but has no measurement and misattributes the cost to the handshake; this supplies the count (21–26/compare) and the dominant term (SSL context construction, not the socket).

findings.title: Every authed request builds 2–3 fresh Supabase clients (4–6 fresh httpx clients + SSL contexts) OUTSIDE the run_db offload, so flipping ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD does not move the expensive half off the loop
findings.evidence: `verify_token` does `client = get_auth_client()` at auth_service.py:256 and only THEN `await run_db(lambda: client.auth.get_user(access_token))` at :257 — the client CONSTRUCTION is outside the offload wrapper. `get_auth_client()` (auth_service.py:30) and `get_user_supabase_client()` (database_service.py:48-53) both call `create_client(...)` unconditionally; only `get_admin_supabase_client()` memoises. Harness `drive_routes.py` counted `supabase.create_client` per request: /auth/verify 1, /auth/me 2, /usage/status 2, /home/savings 2, /home/smart-pick 2, /home/trending 2, /profile/* 2 each, /comparisons/history 3. gc-count: each `create_client` builds 1 httpx.Client eagerly (gotrue) + 1 more on the first `.table()` (postgrest) = 2 SSL contexts. `drive_routes_real.py` (real clients, network severed): a single authed request that got only as far as verify_token still spent 362–808 ms wall with exactly 1 httpx.Client + 1 `load_verify_locations`.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/perf/drive_routes.py out.json  (counts) ; python scratchpad/perf/drive_routes_real.py out.json  (real construction, network severed at httpx.HTTPTransport) ; python scratchpad/perf/m_create_client.py out.json  (334 ms p50 per create_client, 243 ms of it load_verify_locations).
findings.impact: Every authenticated request — including the mobile app's boot-time /auth/verify and its /usage/status and /home/* polls — pays 2–3 Supabase client constructions = 4–6 certifi CA-bundle parses, synchronously, on the single event loop, in ADDITION to the Supabase Auth round trip that `verify_token` makes on every request with no positive-result cache. M13-05's whole point was to get this path off the loop; because the wrapper starts one line too late, ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD=true moves the network wait off the loop and leaves the CPU on it. Dev-box ms (334 ms/client) are Windows/off-lock; Railway is UNMEASURED. The count is not.
findings.fix: Memoise the anon client the way the admin client already is: a module-level `_anon_client` in auth_service (`get_auth_client`) and in database_service, and make `get_user_supabase_client(token)` reuse ONE shared client, applying the per-request JWT via `client.postgrest.auth(token)` on a per-call `headers` copy rather than by constructing a whole client (or, if per-request isolation is required for RLS safety, at minimum pass a shared module-level `ssl.SSLContext` so the CA parse happens once per process). Separately, move `client = get_auth_client()` INSIDE the `run_db` lambda so the construction rides the offload when the flag is on. Cache positive `verify_token` results in Redis keyed by a token hash with a TTL bounded by the JWT `exp` — that removes both the client build and the Supabase RTT from the steady-state authed request.
findings.test_first: tests/test_auth_client_memoised.py: patch `app.services.auth_service.create_client` with a counter, `await verify_token('a')` then `await verify_token('b')`, assert counter == 1. RED today (== 2). Second test: patch `ssl.SSLContext.load_verify_locations`, drive `GET /api/v1/usage/status` twice through TestClient with real clients, assert no growth.
findings.dedupe: new — adjacent to known:#71 (Redis/Supabase off loop) and M13-05, but both of those are about the blocking .execute()/RTT; nobody has noted that the CLIENT CONSTRUCTION sits outside run_db and is the larger CPU term. #73's site list does not include the supabase-py internal httpx clients.

findings.title: Shopify catalog + /meta.json are fetched TWICE per domain on a cold compare — the two products' fan-outs both miss the same cache key with no single-flight
findings.evidence: `_fetch_shopify_catalog` (price_service.py:14305) is a plain read-through cache: `cached = get_cached(cache_key)` at :14318, fetch `https://{domain}/products.json` at :14332, then `data['_store_currency'] = await _fetch_shopify_currency(domain)` (a second GET, /meta.json) at :14361, then `set_cached(...)` at :14363. No in-flight map. COLD compare counts (drive_compare.py): `asyncio.to_thread` -> `_fetch_shopify_catalog.<locals>.<lambda>` x18 and `_fetch_shopify_currency.<locals>.<lambda>` x16; Redis `shopify_catalog:<domain>` GET x2 AND SETEX x2 for each of 9 distinct domains (shopalmoayyed.com, sonyworld.bh, bh.jashanmal.com, imachines.bh, emsquarebh.com, gamerspoint.bh, bhplus.shop, digitalzone.qa, xstore.qa), every GET from the same site `cache_service.py:521 <- price_service.py:14390`. WARM run: exactly x1 per domain — confirming the duplication is precisely the cold-miss race between the two products started by the Phase-1 `asyncio.gather` (scs:3327).
findings.repro: python scratchpad/perf/drive_compare.py out.json cold — compare the `duplicates` block of the cold run (x2 per shopify_catalog key) against the warm run (x1).
findings.impact: 9 duplicate `/products.json` fetches + 8 duplicate `/meta.json` fetches = 17 wasted external HTTP round trips per cold compare, each dispatched into the 40-slot executor, plus 9 duplicate Upstash SETs of a full store catalog. `/products.json?limit=250` is routinely hundreds of KB to several MB, so this is the largest single source of wasted egress and executor occupancy in a cold compare, and it lands inside the 15 s price race. It also doubles the chance of tripping a storefront's rate limit / bot wall from the shared Railway egress IP.
findings.fix: Add a module-level single-flight map to price_service: `_SHOPIFY_INFLIGHT: Dict[str, asyncio.Task]`. In `_fetch_shopify_catalog`, after the cache miss, `task = _SHOPIFY_INFLIGHT.get(domain)`; if absent create it with `asyncio.ensure_future(_do_fetch(domain))` and register a done-callback that pops the key; then `await asyncio.shield(task)` (shield so one caller's 15 s wait_for cancel does not kill the other's fetch). Same pattern for `_fetch_shopify_currency`. Bound the map and clear it per-event-loop. While there, route the `get_cached`/`set_cached` on :14318/:14363 through an offload-aware dispatch (they are raw blocking calls today — see CR-PERFORMANCE-07) and add a size guard before the SET, since a multi-MB catalog can silently exceed Upstash's 1 MB value cap and make the miss permanent.
findings.test_first: tests/test_shopify_catalog_single_flight.py: stub `curl_requests.get` with a counter and a 50 ms sleep, `await asyncio.gather(_fetch_shopify_catalog('d.com'), _fetch_shopify_catalog('d.com'))` against an empty cache, assert the counter == 1. RED today (== 2).

Flag OFF -> inline, byte-identical') but `get_reviews` then calls the raw `cached = get_cached(cache_key)` at :666 and `set_cached(cache_key, db_reviews, REVIEWS_CACHE_TTL)` at :677 — no dispatch. usage_service defines `_get_redis_count_async` at :300-304 but `check_usage_allowed` uses the sync `_get_redis_count` at :652 and :653, and `get_usage_status` uses it at :726 and :727. The two pre-check awaits at 4704/4705 are additionally SEQUENTIAL for two independent keys, so under ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD they become two serial executor hops instead of one gather.

It scales linearly with the number of adapters actually reaching a provider — the roadmap adds virginmegastore/Alshaya/Algolia (#76) and the sitemap channel (#75), so this grows with the source registry rather than staying flat. Upstash RTT from Railway is UNMEASURED, so the ms is MODELLED at 10–30 ms per call.
findings.fix: Make `record_success` a no-op unless the caller already knows the breaker was non-CLOSED. `is_circuit_closed` has just read and parsed the state a few milliseconds earlier — have it stash the parsed state on a ContextVar (or return it) and have `record_success(provider, prior_state=None)` skip the GET entirely when `prior_state` says CLOSED with `failure_count == 0`, which is the only case where the write is pointless. Keep the old GET on the `prior_state is None` path so every existing caller stays byte-identical.
findings.test_first: tests/test_circuit_record_success_noop.py: patch `_redis_get` with a counter, `is_circuit_closed('algolia')` (no state) then `record_success('algolia')`, assert counter == 1. RED today (== 2).

findings.title: 108 of 141 .execute() sites are outside run_db — every /home/* and /profile/* request-path read stays on the event loop even with ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD flipped ON
findings.evidence: AST/text scan of every .py in app/ at 76ace90 (`scan_exec.py`): 141 `.execute()` sites, 33 inside a `run_db(` window, 108 bare. Request-path bare sites: home_routes.py:616 and :659 (`/home/smart-pick` — `users.select('preferences, behavior_profile').single()` then `comparisons.select('id, full_response, created_at').limit(5)`), home_routes.py:828 (`/home/trending` region fallback), profile_routes.py:196, :322, :344, :487 (all three `/profile/*` endpoints), database_service.py:600 (`get_user_demographics`, awaited on the compare critical path), auth_routes.py:381/391/881/958/963, plus 31 in referral_service.py and 22 in admin_routes.py. Harness counts confirm these fire: /home/smart-pick 2 executes, /profile/monthly-stats 2, /profile/recent-decisions 1, /home/trending 1, all with 2 `create_client` each.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/perf/scan_exec.py out.json  (prints TOTAL 141 wrapped 33 bare 108 and the per-file bare line numbers). python scratchpad/perf/drive_routes.py out.json for the per-route execute counts.
findings.impact: M13-05 built `run_db` explicitly so a burst of concurrent DB round trips could not convert into hard-cap timeouts for unrelated requests on the single-worker uvicorn. The offload covers the compare path reasonably (5 of 6 scs sites, all of usage_service's consume path, save_comparison, log_search) but NOT the four screens the app loads on every app-open: home/savings' sibling endpoints, all three profile endpoints, and `get_user_demographics` on the compare critical path. So the answer to 'what changes when the offload flags flip' is: 7 request-path queries across 5 endpoints do not move. This is a coverage gap in a shipped mitigation, not a new mechanism.
findings.fix: Wrap the seven request-path sites in `await run_db(lambda: ...)` — mechanical, and flag-OFF is byte-identical by `run_db`'s own contract (an `async def` with no `await` on the inline branch). Do home_routes.py:616, :659, :828, profile_routes.py:196, :322, :344, :487 and database_service.py:600 in one pass. Leave admin_routes (admin-key gated, not user-facing) and referral_service (needs its own triage — 31 sites) for a follow-up. Add a lint/test that fails when a new bare `.execute()` appears under app/api/ or on a request-path service function.
findings.test_first: tests/test_run_db_coverage.py: AST-walk app/api/home_routes.py and app/api/profile_routes.py, assert every `.execute()` call has a `run_db` ancestor in the enclosing statement. RED today (7 sites).
findings.dedupe: new — extends known:#71 / M13-05, which established the mechanism and the flag; nobody has audited the flag's actual coverage.

findings.title: All 9 BeautifulSoup sites use the slow pure-Python html.parser while lxml 6.1.2 is already pinned in requirements — and M13-50 recommends DELETING that dependency
findings.evidence: Every soup in price_service is built with the default pure-Python parser: `BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')` at :10642, :12432, :13056, :13869, :14789, :14925, :14983, :15082, :15425. `requirements.txt:93` pins `lxml==6.1.2` and `requirements.in:24` declares `lxml>=5.0.0`; lxml 6.0.2 is importable in this env. MEASURED on the same corpus pages: 583,231 B page — html.parser 158.7 ms vs lxml 55.9 ms (2.84x); 175,993 B — 26.3 vs 21.8; 183,366 B — 17.1 vs 13.0; 120,798 B — 17.5 vs 19.8; 172,527 B — 23.8 vs 24.0. cProfile of 10 pages: 88.6% of `extract_price_from_html`'s cumulative time is inside bs4/html.parser (`goahead` 4.282 s, `parse_starttag` 52,300 calls). Meanwhile `docs/investigations/2026-08-31-m13-full-review.md:79` (M13-50, P2) says lxml is an 'unused direct runtime dependency' and recommends dropping it.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/perf/m_soup.py out.json (see `parser_compare`). python scratchpad/perf/prof_extract.py out.txt for the cProfile top-20.
findings.impact: The gain is concentrated exactly where it matters: the big pages. Small PDPs are a wash, but 583 KB+ pages — the Cloudflare-fronted GCC storefronts the Tier-1.5 cascade escalates to — are ~2.8x faster, i.e. ~100 ms of loop-blocking CPU recovered per large page. Combined with CR-PERFORMANCE-01 (4 parses -> 1), a 550 ms page becomes roughly 50 ms. Acting on M13-50 as written would delete the dependency that makes this free, so this finding needs to reach whoever owns that issue before the dependency prune lands. This also supplies the measurement M18's LS-capacity-math-05 was downgraded to P3 for lacking ('100-300ms/page has no measurement anywhere in the repo' — measured: 93–550 ms/page, median 217 ms, 10 pages).
findings.fix: Introduce one helper `_soup(html)` in price_service that tries `BeautifulSoup(html, 'lxml')` and falls back to `'html.parser'` on ImportError/FeatureNotFound, and route all 9 sites through it behind ENABLE_LXML_PARSER (default OFF for one deploy, then ON). lxml is more lenient about malformed markup in some places and stricter in others, so gate it and validate with the existing byte-identity corpus gate over `_proof/html` before flipping. Do NOT drop lxml per M13-50 until this is decided — comment on that issue.
findings.test_first: tests/test_soup_parser_parity.py: for each of ~30 `_proof/html` pages, assert `extract_price_from_html(...)` returns the identical dict under ENABLE_LXML_PARSER on and off. RED (or at least informative) today because the flag does not exist; it is the gate the flip needs.
findings.dedupe: known:M18/LS-capacity-math-05 — still-open (downgraded P2->P3 for lack of measurement; measurement supplied here, and its central factual correction stands: the parse runs ON the loop, not in executor threads). The parser choice itself and the M13-50 contradiction are new.

findings.title: /home/savings flag-OFF full scan: measured cost formula is N x 17.9 KB of wire + JSON decode, so a 10k-row user pulls ~180 MB into a 0.14 GB-RSS worker
findings.evidence: Flag-OFF branch at home_routes.py:249-256 selects `full_response` for ALL of a user's schema_version=2 rows with no limit, then scans them in Python (:262-276). `_home_savings_aggregate_enabled()` (home_routes.py:55-65) is default OFF and ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE is absent from the Railway `web` variable list, and migrations/036_home_savings_aggregate.sql is UNAPPLIED — so the scan is what ships today. MEASURED inputs (Supabase SELECT only, `m_fullresponse.py`): 27 rows, full_response avg 17,936 B / p50 19,026 B / max 24,975 B; heaviest user has 10 rows; the Python side of the scan is negligible (`_extract_winner_loser_prices` 0.0008 ms/row), and `json.loads` of the largest payload is 0.177 ms.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/perf/m_fullresponse.py out.json ; python scratchpad/perf/drive_routes.py out.json (GET /api/v1/home/savings -> 1 supabase.execute, 2 create_client, 2 redis.get, 1 redis.setex).
findings.impact: MODELLED from measured per-row constants: N=10 (today's worst user) = 179 KB wire, ~2 ms decode — invisible. N=1,000 = 17.9 MB, ~190 ms decode. N=10,000 = 179 MB, ~1.9 s decode. N=100,000 = 1.8 GB, ~19 s decode — an OOM on a service whose measured RSS is 0.1356 GB. The 6 h TTL with bust-on-write amortises it, but every comparison SAVE busts the key, so an active user re-pays the full scan on their next home-screen load; a user who compares daily pays it daily and the cost grows monotonically with their lifetime history. The SELECT is run_db-wrapped so the wait moves off-loop under ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD, but the postgrest decode of the whole array does not.
findings.fix: This is already designed and written — apply migrations/036_home_savings_aggregate.sql, verify the RPC against the 27 real rows, then set ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE=true on the `web` service. Until that lands, cap the legacy branch: add `.order('created_at', desc=True).limit(500)` and stamp `"truncated": true` on the payload, so the failure mode is an understated banner rather than an OOM. Do not extend the flag-OFF branch otherwise — the code comment at :246-248 already says so.
findings.test_first: tests/test_home_savings_bounded.py: stub the client to return 5,000 synthetic rows of ~18 KB each, call the flag-OFF branch, assert the recorded query carries a bounded `.limit(...)` and that the handler does not materialise more than the cap. RED today (unbounded).
findings.dedupe: known:#116 + M18/LS-event-loop-01 — still-open (flag default OFF, migration 036 unapplied, absent from Railway vars). Fresh: the measured per-row constants (avg 17,936 B, decode 0.177 ms/25 KB) that turn the known shape into a cost curve.

findings.title: P3 sweep: per-request costs that are NOT defects, plus four small redundancies
findings.evidence: CLEARED (measured, no defect — recorded so nobody re-checks): (1) `get_comparison_service()` builds a new StructuredComparisonService per request but `__init__` (scs:2602-2653) only assigns dicts/None — MEASURED 0.26 us per construction over 1000 iterations; not a cost. (2) AsyncOpenAI is NOT constructed per request: openai_service.py:32 is module-level and :61/:70 memoise into `_client_cache` (:43); extraction_service.py:51 and url_extraction_service.py:31 are lazy singletons — MEASURED 0 constructions across 10 `get_client()` calls and 0 on the warm compare (1 on the cold, the first-ever build). (3) full_response (de)serialisation is ~3 passes per compare (FastAPI jsonable_encoder + json.dumps on the response, one more inside the fire-and-forget save) — MEASURED 0.646 ms + 0.073 ms for a real 16,555 B payload; ~1 ms/request, not a bottleneck. (4) No unbounded module-level mutable in app/services: all 8 candidates with writers are domain-keyed or self-capped (`robots_eval._RX_CACHE` capped at 4,000 at :159-161; `spec_spine._STORE_CACHE` calls `.clear()` before each insert at :186; `openai_service._client_cache` holds 2), and all 6 lru_cache sites are maxsize<=2048. No leak. (5) No duplicate Serper QUERY within a compare: 22 calls / 22 distinct (cold), 19 / 19 (warm). (6) In-function regexes: 120 `re.*` calls sit inside function bodies (63 in price_service) but all use literal patterns that CPython's 512-entry re cache serves, and the 8 in-function `re.compile` sites are either literal (price_service.py:8464, url_extraction_service.py:150/157) or behind their own memo (robots_eval.py:159, review_service.py:490). Not a hot-path cost. STILL WORTH FIXING (small): (a) `get_user_demographics` (database_service.py:600) selects `users.demographics_profile` while `_fetch_behavior_profile` (scs:3322) selects `users.behavior_profile` from the SAME row — two Supabase queries and two client builds where one `select('behavior_profile, demographics_profile')` would do; MEASURED `users|select,eq,single` x2 per authed compare, and the demographics one is additionally bare (not run_db-wrapped). (b) scs:4704/4705 await two independent Redis reads sequentially instead of gathering them. (c) `extract_price_from_html` does `from bs4 import BeautifulSoup` inside the function body (price_service.py:13012) — a sys.modules lookup per call, trivial but pointless. (d) `_fetch_shopify_catalog`'s cache read/write (price_service.py:14318/:14363) use the raw blocking `get_cached`/`set_cached`, so they are invisible to ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD.

findings.title: comparison_feedback.winner_correct has no writer anywhere in the codebase, and it is the ONLY quality filter the few-shot rotation cron applies — the exemplar miner can never find a row
findings.evidence: Ran the real function: `cron_few_shot_rotation._fetch_top_decile_feedback -> 0 rows`. Live probe: `comparison_feedback?select=id&winner_correct=not.is.null` -> content-range `*/0`. grep for winner_correct across app/ finds ZERO writers; FeedbackRequest (feedback_routes.py:87-91) has only useful/comparison_id/mattered_most/change_suggestion.
findings.repro: cd repo; python -c "import asyncio;from dotenv import load_dotenv;load_dotenv('.env',override=True);from app.services.database_service import get_admin_supabase_client;from scripts.cron_few_shot_rotation import _fetch_top_decile_feedback;print(len(asyncio.run(_fetch_top_decile_feedback(get_admin_supabase_client()))))" -> 0. Then curl the live REST: GET /rest/v1/comparison_feedback?select=id&winner_correct=not.is.null with Prefer: count=exact -> */0.
findings.impact: Migration 027 added winner_correct/price_correct/specs_correct plus a partial index in June; the per-axis UI it was written for ('until B.3 wires the per-axis UI', 027 line ~66) never landed, so all three columns are 100% NULL in prod (measured: 0 of 1 rows non-null). _fetch_top_decile_feedback filters `.eq("useful",True).eq("winner_correct","correct")` — an AND over a column that is always NULL — so the moment ENABLE_FEWSHOT_ROTATION is flipped the rotation will run, mine zero exemplars, and log nothing that says why. The prompt-exemplar refresh loop is therefore permanently inert and will look like 'no good feedback yet' rather than 'the column is never written'. DARK FLAG: ENABLE_FEWSHOT_ROTATION is absent from the Railway `web` and `price-warmer` variable sets (baseline/railway-web-vars.txt), so this is unreachable today — severity capped at P2 per the brief.
findings.fix: Two-part. (a) Land the writer: add optional `winner_correct`/`price_correct`/`specs_correct` (3-state 'correct'|'wrong'|'unsure', matching the 027 CHECK) to FeedbackRequest in app/api/feedback_routes.py and pass them into save_feedback's `record` in app/services/feedback_service.py:139-152, guarded by a new default-OFF flag ENABLE_PER_AXIS_FEEDBACK so the mobile app can ship the UI on its own clock. (b) Until (a) has data, make the miner degrade honestly: in _fetch_top_decile_feedback, drop the `.eq("winner_correct","correct")` filter to a preference (fetch on `useful=true`, then rank rows that carry winner_correct='correct' first) and emit a WARNING when zero rows carry a non-null per-axis signal, so the cron says 'no per-axis feedback exists' instead of silently producing an empty rotation. Do not flip ENABLE_FEWSHOT_ROTATION before (a) has landed and at least _MIN_EXEMPLARS_PER_CATEGORY rows exist.
findings.test_first: tests/test_feedback_axis_persistence.py::test_winner_correct_round_trips — POST /api/v1/feedback with winner_correct='correct' through the real route, then assert the value comes back on the inserted comparison_feedback record; RED today because FeedbackRequest rejects/drops the field. Pair it with tests/test_few_shot_rotation.py::test_fetch_top_decile_returns_rows_when_only_useful_is_set — stub a client whose comparison_feedback table has useful=true and winner_correct=None and assert _fetch_top_decile_feedback returns it (or at minimum logs a warning); RED today because the .eq filter drops it.

findings.title: Every analytics_service dashboard query is unbounded and silently truncated at PostgREST max-rows=1000 — 'popular queries' is ranked from 6% of search_logs, in arbitrary physical order
findings.evidence: MEASURED cap: GET /rest/v1/search_logs?select=query,input_type -> HTTP 206, content-range `0-999/16283`. Ran the real functions: get_popular_queries top-1 = {'query':'iPhone 15 vs Galaxy S24','count':369}; raw unbounded select returned 1000 rows of 16283; get_daily_stats(days=120) -> total_comparisons=1000 with only 13 days in daily_breakdown.
findings.repro: cd repo; python -c "import asyncio;from dotenv import load_dotenv;load_dotenv('.env',override=True);from app.services import analytics_service as a;print(asyncio.run(a.get_popular_queries(5)));print(asyncio.run(a.get_daily_stats(120))['total_comparisons'])" -> the 120-day total prints 1000 even though search_logs holds 13,237 rows since 2026-06-01 (baseline/search_logs_summary.txt).
findings.impact: Four dashboards are wrong, not merely stale: get_popular_queries (line 65, NO filter at all), get_daily_stats (line 19), get_cost_trends (line 87) and get_error_stats (line 126) all issue filter-only selects with no .limit()/.range() and no ORDER BY. PostgREST answers 206 with the first 1000 rows in whatever order the planner returns, and supabase-py surfaces that as an ordinary success — no exception, no truncation flag, no log line. So /admin/analytics reports total_comparisons=1000 for any window with more than 1000 rows (June alone had 9,157), total_cost is the cost of an arbitrary 1000-row slice, and the 'top queries' ranking is computed over ~6% of the corpus with no guarantee the slice is recent. Every historical cost/error-rate number a human read off this dashboard since the row count crossed 1000 is understated by an unknown factor. Not user-facing (admin only), hence P2 rather than P1.
findings.fix: Two changes, both unflagged corrections. (1) For the three windowed functions, add `.order("created_at", desc=True)` and page explicitly with `.range(offset, offset+999)` in a loop until a short page comes back, or better, replace the Python-side Counter with a server-side aggregate (the same pattern migration 036 uses for /home/savings: a SECURITY DEFINER SQL function `search_log_daily_rollup(p_since timestamptz)` returning day/count/cost/success_count, GRANTed to service_role only, whose cost does not grow with the table). (2) For get_popular_queries, which has no window at all, add a `.gte("created_at", since)` bound plus the same rollup, since ranking all-time queries by scanning the table will only get worse. In every case, compare `len(records)` against the exact count (`count="exact"`) and surface a `truncated: true` field in the response so a partial answer is never presented as a total.

findings.title: Six live tables have no DDL in migrations/ at all — including user_events and comparison_feedback, whose only user_id query pattern has no index defined anywhere in version control
findings.evidence: 22 CREATE TABLE statements across 30 migration files cover 16 of the 22 live base tables. Live-but-undefined: users, comparisons, comparison_feedback, user_events, bahrain_approved_drugs, rating_cache. 010 ALTERs and adds policies to users/comparisons/search_logs/comparison_feedback/user_events without ever creating them; 001 is '001_UPDATE_comparisons.sql'.
findings.repro: static. `grep -h 'CREATE TABLE' migrations/*.sql` at 76ace90 lists 22 statements; diff that set against the 22 base tables in the live OpenAPI definitions (GET /rest/v1/, Accept: application/openapi+json). The 46 CREATE INDEX statements contain no index on user_events or comparison_feedback; the only comparison_feedback index (027:67) is a partial index on created_at gated on the three all-NULL correctness columns, so it indexes zero rows.
findings.impact: The schema of the six busiest user-data tables lives only in the Supabase dashboard. Concretely: (a) nobody can rebuild a staging or CI database from migrations/ — a fresh apply produces a schema on which 010/011 fail immediately; (b) the index situation is unknowable from the repo, and for the two tables that matter it is unknowable AND undefined — structured_comparison_service.py:4546 filters comparison_feedback by user_id and :4547 filters user_events by user_id with `order(created_at desc).limit(200)`, and admin_routes.py:375 runs user_events `.eq(user_id).limit(50)` once PER USER inside a loop; none of those access paths has an index in version control; (c) constraint drift is invisible — this project has already been burned once by exactly this (migration 017's header documents comparisons.share_token silently being varchar(12) in prod against 22-char tokens, breaking sharing from Session 22 to 42 with 0 of 6 comparisons carrying a token). user_events is at 146 rows and comparison_feedback at 1 today, so there is no live latency harm — this is a correctness-of-the-record and future-growth finding, P2.
findings.fix: Add a single `migrations/000_baseline_schema.sql` capturing the current live DDL for users, comparisons, comparison_feedback, user_events, bahrain_approved_drugs and rating_cache — pull it from the Supabase dashboard's schema export (or `pg_dump --schema-only -t`) rather than reconstructing it by hand, mark it 'baseline: already applied in prod, present so a fresh environment can be built', and make every statement IF NOT EXISTS so re-applying is a no-op. In the same file add the two missing access-path indexes: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_events_user_created ON user_events (user_id, created_at DESC);` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_comparison_feedback_user ON comparison_feedback (user_id);`. Both are additive and safe on tables of this size. Note the live index state cannot be read through PostgREST (see not_covered), so apply with IF NOT EXISTS and confirm in the dashboard.

RED today on six tables. findings.title: Migrations 010/011/012 are non-idempotent (bare CREATE POLICY / CREATE INDEX) so a re-run aborts the Supabase SQL editor's single transaction, and rollback/ has parity only from 023 onward
findings.evidence: 010 issues 10 bare `CREATE POLICY` statements (lines 17-64) with no DROP IF EXISTS; 011 has `CREATE INDEX idx_usage_user_period` (line 23) and `CREATE POLICY usage_select/usage_insert/usage_update/audit_insert` bare; 012 has 6 bare CREATE INDEX + 8 bare CREATE POLICY. From 014 onward every file uses the DROP-then-CREATE / IF NOT EXISTS pattern and says why ('PG15 has no CREATE POLICY IF NOT EXISTS').
findings.repro: static. `grep -n 'CREATE POLICY\|CREATE INDEX' migrations/010_enable_rls.sql migrations/011_security_completion_freemium.sql migrations/012_product_data_tables.sql` — none is preceded by a DROP ... IF EXISTS and none carries IF NOT EXISTS. `ls migrations/rollback/` returns 15 files, the lowest numbered being 023.
findings.impact: Two hygiene gaps with the same root. (1) Re-running 010, 011 or 012 in the Supabase SQL editor raises 42710 'policy already exists' / 42P07 'relation already exists' on the first duplicate; because the editor wraps a multi-statement script in ONE transaction (a fact migration 036's own header calls out: 'a later failure silently rolls back earlier statements'), the operator gets a rollback of everything that ran before it and an ambiguous partial state to reason about. That is precisely the trap 014+ were written to avoid, and 010-012 were never backfilled. (2) rollback/ covers 023-036 but nothing for 010-022, so there is no documented undo for the entire RLS baseline, the product-data L2 tables or the referral system. Neither is a live defect — capped P3 — but both raise the cost of the next schema recovery, and this project has already lost a feature to schema drift once (017's post-mortem).
findings.fix: Backfill idempotence into 010/011/012 exactly as 014 does: prefix every `CREATE POLICY x ON t` with `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS x ON t;` and change every `CREATE INDEX y` to `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS y`. This is a pure edit to already-applied files, so it changes nothing in prod but makes a replay safe. Then add rollback/ files for 010-022 following the shape of rollback/023_referral_lifetime_cap_ROLLBACK.sql — at minimum for 012 (the product-data tables) and 014 (the referral system), the two with real data behind them. Finally, wrap 010/011/012 in explicit BEGIN;/COMMIT; the way 025-036 do, so the transaction boundary is in the file rather than implied by the editor.
findings.test_first: tests/test_migration_idempotence.py::test_every_migration_is_replay_safe — read each migrations/*.sql, strip comments, and assert every CREATE POLICY has a matching DROP POLICY IF EXISTS earlier in the file and every CREATE INDEX / CREATE TABLE carries IF NOT EXISTS. RED today on 010, 011, 012. Extend tests/test_migration_index_predicate_immutability.py (which already comment-strips) rather than adding a new harness. A second test asserts every migrations/NNN_*.sql numbered >= 010 has a migrations/rollback/NNN_*.sql sibling — RED on 010-022.

findings.title: No retention or cleanup exists for any append-only table (search_logs 16,283 rows and growing, product_prices 3,945), and the one cleanup function that IS deployed is called by zero code
findings.evidence: Live counts: search_logs 16283, product_prices 3945, admin_audit_log 1439, product_reviews 627, product_specs 643, user_events 146. `grep -rn 'retention|purge|prune|DELETE FROM|cleanup_expired'` over app/ + scripts/ finds only per-user deletes (delete_comparison, delete_user_cascade). Live RPC `cleanup_expired_ratings` exists; ZERO call sites in the repo.
findings.repro: HEAD /rest/v1/<table>?select=id with Prefer: count=exact for each of 21 tables (counts above). `grep -rn 'cleanup_expired_ratings' app/ scripts/` -> no match, while the function is present in the live OpenAPI /rpc paths. `grep -rn 'DELETE FROM' migrations/` -> only inside delete_user_cascade (010:77-80, 025:36-51).
findings.impact: Four tables are pure append with no TTL and no sweeper: search_logs (one row per compare — 16,283 rows for ~27 saved comparisons, so it is the highest-volume table by an order of magnitude and it stores raw user query text plus error strings indefinitely), product_prices (one row per L2 price fetch, deliberately append-only 'keeps history', 3,945 rows), admin_audit_log (1,439), and user_events. Nothing deletes them and nothing alerts on their size. Two consequences beyond disk: the retention gap is a privacy exposure (search_logs.query holds free-text user input forever, and delete_user_cascade only removes rows where user_id matches — anonymous rows, which are the majority given 12,505 'text' inputs against 18 users, are never reachable by a deletion request); and the growth silently worsens CR-DATA-MIGRATIONS-04, since every crossing of a 1000-row boundary makes another dashboard number quietly wrong. Volumes are small today and traffic is ~zero (Railway: 16 requests sampled in 24h), so P3.
findings.fix: Add a `migrations/037_retention.sql` defining one SECURITY DEFINER sweeper per table with an explicit window — e.g. `search_logs_prune(p_days int default 180)` deleting created_at < now() - interval, `product_prices_prune(p_days int default 90)` keeping the newest row per (product_key, region) regardless of age so the L2 cache is never emptied, and `admin_audit_log_prune(p_days int default 365)` — each REVOKEd from PUBLIC and GRANTed to service_role only, mirroring 036's lockdown. Wire them into a new `scripts/cron_retention.py` behind a default-OFF ENABLE_RETENTION_SWEEP so the first run is a deliberate flip, and log the deleted row count. Separately, either call the already-deployed cleanup_expired_ratings from that cron or drop the function — a deployed-but-uncalled SECURITY DEFINER routine is unnecessary attack surface.

RED today: no sweeper exists. Pair with tests/test_no_orphan_db_functions.py::test_every_live_rpc_has_a_call_site — assert every function name in the live /rpc OpenAPI paths appears in a `.rpc("...")` literal in app/ or scripts/; RED today on cleanup_expired_ratings.

findings.title: STATUS M13-29 RLS gap still open by design: /events still writes through the service-role client, so the only control on a forged comparison_id is a UUID format check — inventory of all RLS policies, SECURITY DEFINER functions and GRANTs
findings.evidence: track_events_batch (:194) and track_event (:180) both call `get_supabase_client()`, which database_service.py:57-61 documents as 'DEPRECATED ... Returns admin client' — service-role, RLS bypassed. feedback_service.py:133-136 states it plainly: 'migrations/010 INSERT policies do not constrain comparison_id, so the user client alone would not stop it (recorded follow-up)'.
findings.repro: static, plus a live read: GET /rest/v1/user_events?select=id&comparison_id=not.is.null -> 27 of 146 rows carry a comparison_id. No write was attempted (read-only rule), so the policy set below is DDL-derived, not exercised.
findings.impact: INVENTORY (cr-security owns the exposure verdict; this is the DDL-vs-call-site map). RLS enabled on 15 tables across 010/011/012/014/028/029/030/031/032/035. Own-row policies: users (select/update/insert on auth.uid()=id), comparisons (select `auth.uid()=user_id OR share_token IS NOT NULL` per 017 — note the OR makes ANY shared row readable by ANY authenticated caller; both history_routes call sites re-check ownership with hmac.compare_digest, so it is contained in code, not in the policy), search_logs/comparison_feedback/user_events (insert `auth.uid()=user_id OR user_id IS NULL`, select own-row only), user_usage, referral_invites/redemptions/deep_review_credits/re_engagement_events (select-own, TO authenticated), pain_workflow_events, user_preference_history. Fully permissive: product_specs/product_prices/product_reviews carry `USING (true)` / `WITH CHECK (true)` for select AND insert (012:19-21,41-42,58-60) — anon-key writes to the L2 price cache are policy-allowed. RLS-enabled-with-no-policy (deny-all except service_role): verdict_critiques (030), eval_runs (031); service-role-only policies: products (032), spec_spine (035). findings.impact: A whole persistence pipeline is dead-wired: migration 002 created products with two indexes, migration 032 enabled RLS and added a service-role-only policy, database_service ships upsert_product + upsert_products_from_comparison, and analytics_service.get_product_stats + the /api/v1/admin/products route read it — but nothing ever calls the writer, so GET /admin/products returns total_products 0 with empty category_breakdown and top_brands, forever. findings.title: "all 28 P1s closed" contradicts "#114 alone stays deliberately unbuilt" inside the same sentence, and a third count lives in the session log
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:449: "...is fully remediated to the edge of what code can do: **all 28 P1s closed** (issues `#97`-`#121`; `#114` alone stays deliberately unbuilt — the mis-keyed limiter is what currently protects the single event loop...)". docs/CONTEXT_SESSION_LOG.md:20 heading for the same work: "SESSION 62: M18 REVIEW -> M20/M21 REMEDIATION — 25 OF 28 P1 FINDINGS CLOSED (24/25 ISSUES; #114 HELD BY DESIGN)". The M22 brief's own dedupe list records "28 P1 — 27 closed, #114 held by design". Three sources, three counts (28/28, 25/28, 27/28).
findings.repro: grep -n '28 P1' CLAUDE.md docs/CONTEXT_SESSION_LOG.md  # static, both files read at HEAD 76ace90
findings.impact: The bolded string is what an agent greps and quotes. "all 28 P1s closed" is the sentence that ends a launch-readiness question, and it is false: #114 (the limiter key anchor) is open, and it is the single item gating the whole rate-limit/offload activation ordering. A session that trusts the bold and skips the parenthesis will either report the campaign as complete or flip ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT believing nothing is outstanding — which CLAUDE.md:357 elsewhere calls a HARD PRECONDITION violation with an attacker-forgeable limiter key. The disagreement also makes the P1 count unusable as a status signal in any future handoff.
findings.fix: Rewrite CLAUDE.md:449 to lead with the true count and the exception, not the round number: "27 of 28 P1s closed (issues #97-#121); **#114 remains OPEN and held by design** — the mis-keyed limiter is what currently protects the single event loop, so it lands only after the offload flags are ACTIVE and Railway's hop count is live-verified." Reconcile the session-log heading (25 of 28) to the same number in the same commit, and state which denominator is findings vs issues since those differ (28 findings / 25 issues). Adopt a standing rule for this file: never write an aggregate claim ('all X closed') in the same sentence as its own exception — state the exception first.

findings.title: settings.local.json permanently allows machine shutdown and blanket `Bash(git *)` with no deny list, so an agent can power off the dev box or force-push without a prompt
findings.evidence: Parsed the file at HEAD: 192 allow entries, and `permissions` has ONLY an `allow` key — no `deny`, no `ask`, no `hooks` anywhere in .claude/. Destructive entries persisted forever: `"Bash(shutdown /s /t 5 /c \"Shutdown by Claude Code per user request — Session 50 wrapped, all work pushed to main.\"")"`, `"Bash(shutdown /s /t 5)"`, `"Bash(MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 shutdown //s //t 5)"`, `"PowerShell(Stop-Computer -Force)"`, `"Bash(powershell -c \"Get-Process python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force\")"`, `"Bash(git reset *)"`. And `"Bash(git *)"` is present, which subsumes all 41 of the file's specific git entries and grants push / reset --hard / checkout / worktree / branch -D unprompted. The three broadest remaining entries are `Bash(python:*)` (arbitrary code execution, subsuming 6 narrower python entries), `Bash(curl:*)` (arbitrary HTTP incl. POST to prod and to paid APIs) and `Bash(node -e *)`. User layer compounds it: ~/.claude/settings.json sets `"skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true`.
findings.repro: python -c "import json;a=json.load(open('.claude/settings.local.json'))['permissions'];print(list(a));print(len(a['allow']));print([x for x in a['allow'] if 'shutdown' in x.lower() or 'Stop-Computer' in x or x=='Bash(git *)'])"
findings.impact: Three of these are unbounded and irreversible from inside a session. `PowerShell(Stop-Computer -Force)` and the three `shutdown /s` variants power off the machine with no prompt — they were approved once for a deliberate end-of-Session-50 wrap and have been standing authority ever since; any agent that decides a reboot would help can take the box down mid-wave with uncommitted worktrees. `Bash(git *)` unprompted covers `git push --force` and `git reset --hard` on a repo whose master is currently 7 commits ahead of origin/main. `Bash(curl:*)` unprompted is a live-write path to prod and to metered third-party APIs, in a repo whose own brief classifies prod writes and paid API calls as prohibited. There is no `deny` list, so nothing protects `.env` (which CLAUDE.md:638 says is the only place full API keys live) from `Bash(python:*)` or `Bash(curl:*)`.
findings.fix: Propose-only, three edits Ahmed makes: (1) delete the four shutdown/Stop-Computer entries and the two Stop-Process entries — a machine power-off should always cost one prompt; (2) replace `Bash(git *)` with the read/act split the workflow actually needs (`Bash(git status:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)`, `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git show:*)`, `Bash(git add:*)`, `Bash(git commit:*)`) and let push/reset/checkout/worktree prompt — that also lets the 41 redundant git entries be deleted; (3) add a `deny` block, which the file has never had, covering at minimum `Read(./.env)`, `Read(./.env.*)`, `Bash(git push --force:*)`, `Bash(git reset --hard:*)` and `Bash(rm -rf:*)`. The user already has the `git-guardrails-claude-code` and `careful`/`guard` skills installed at ~/.claude/skills/ that generate exactly this hook set — none of them has been applied to this repo (0 hooks configured).
findings.test_first: `tests/test_claude_permissions.py::test_no_destructive_permissions` — load .claude/settings.local.json and assert no allow entry matches `shutdown|Stop-Computer|Stop-Process|^Bash\(git \*\)$`, and assert `permissions.deny` exists and contains an `.env` read rule. RED at HEAD on both halves.

findings.title: settings.local.json is git-tracked and not gitignored, so 192 allow rules including machine-shutdown propagate to every clone and worktree
findings.evidence: `git ls-files .claude/` returns `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json` and the 4 SKILL.md files — the `.local` file IS tracked. `Select-String .gitignore -Pattern 'claude|settings'` returns nothing, so it is not ignored either. `git log -1 -- .claude/settings.local.json` = `2b11f4f 2026-05-22` — it has not been curated in 3.5 months while accumulating to 192 entries. The `.local.json` suffix is Claude Code's per-machine/personal settings convention; the shared, reviewable file is `.claude/settings.json`, which here contains only 78 bytes (one plugin enablement).

findings.title: The typescript-lsp plugin CLAUDE.md blames for fabricating errors five times in one day is still enabled at the user layer; the fix is prose re-read every session instead of a config change
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:65: "IDE/LSP TS diagnostics on Windows are unreliable (`typescript-lsp` plugin bug, see MEMORY.md). Trust ONLY `npx tsc --noEmit` exit code — ignore stale 'Cannot find module' / 'JSX flag not set' errors from system-reminders unless `tsc` actually fails." CLAUDE.md:453 escalates it: "**The Windows IDE/LSP diagnostics fabricated errors five times in one day** (incl. fake syntax errors). Trust ONLY `npx tsc --noEmit` + jest; this extends the existing Frontend-section warning to ALL diagnostics." The user auto-memory index repeats it a third time ("IDE diagnostics fabricated errors 5x (trust ONLY tsc+jest)"). Config at HEAD: ~/.claude/settings.json `enabledPlugins` contains `"typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true`, and ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json shows it installed at user scope, version 1.0.0, since 2026-03-18. Baseline measurement confirms the plugin's diagnostics are the unreliable half: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 and jest 2320 passed / 242 suites at HEAD.
findings.repro: python -c "import json;print(json.load(open(r'C:/Users/SynAckITPC/.claude/settings.json'))['enabledPlugins']['typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official'])"  # -> True ; grep -n 'typescript-lsp' CLAUDE.md  # -> :65
findings.impact: A known-bad tool is left switched on and the mitigation is a warning that has to be re-read, re-believed and re-applied by every agent, every session, three times over in three documents — and it still failed five times in one day. The failure mode is expensive in both directions: an agent that trusts a fabricated error rewrites working code (CLAUDE.md records fake syntax errors), and an agent trained to ignore all diagnostics will also ignore a real one. The always-on cost is real too: ~600 bytes of CLAUDE.md plus a slot in the user memory index are spent restating a workaround for a plugin that could simply be off.
findings.fix: Turn the prose mitigation into a config change at the layer where the problem lives (user layer, ~/.claude/settings.json): set `"typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official": false`. TypeScript ground truth in this repo is already `npx tsc --noEmit` (CI job frontend-typecheck, blocking, and the frontend-tests job runs it again), so disabling the plugin removes the fabrication source and loses no capability. If Ahmed wants to keep it for editor navigation, then reduce the CLAUDE.md footprint to a single line at the Frontend section and delete the duplicate at :453 and the memory-index copy — one statement of a rule is more likely to be followed than three. Either way this is Ahmed's call on his own user settings; I am proposing, not changing.
findings.test_first: Not unit-testable (user-layer config, outside the repo). The falsifiable check is a documented one-liner in the runbook: `python -c "import json;print(json.load(open(SETTINGS))['enabledPlugins'].get('typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official'))"` must print `False` before the CLAUDE.md warning is deleted.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md still describes the frontend-tests CI job as non-blocking `continue-on-error`; at HEAD that ratchet is already complete and jest/eslint/tsc are blocking
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:529 (M13-W4 findings list, M13-16): "the FIRST frontend CI job — `frontend-tests`: `npm ci` -> `jest --ci` -> `eslint src` -> `tsc --noEmit`, each **non-blocking** `continue-on-error`; ratchet each to blocking once its CI red count is measured", reinforced at :530 "(3) frontend-static — CI YAML parses, job non-blocking" and "which is exactly why the CI job lands non-blocking to MEASURE them on a runner". Ground truth at HEAD: .github/workflows/ci.yml has `continue-on-error` at exactly two places, lines 157 (black whole-repo drift report) and 199 (npm audit) — NOT in the frontend-tests job, whose steps are :263 `npx jest --ci`, :269 `npx eslint "src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"`, :273 `npx tsc --noEmit`, all bare. The job's own header comment at :240 says the ratchet is done. The user memory index agrees ("CI green (all 5 jobs REQUIRED)").
findings.repro: grep -n 'continue-on-error' .github/workflows/ci.yml  # -> 157, 199 only ; sed -n '247,275p' .github/workflows/ci.yml ; grep -n 'non-blocking' CLAUDE.md  # -> 529, 530
findings.impact: The always-on doc understates the merge gate. An agent that reads CLAUDE.md before pushing believes jest, eslint and tsc failures are advisory and will push a branch that CI then rejects — wasting a cycle — or, worse, will treat a red frontend job as expected noise and merge past it. It also mis-prices the value of the eslint baseline: at HEAD eslint is 0 errors / 152 warnings, which only matters as a gate if the step is blocking. This is the same failure class as finding 05: a status claim in CLAUDE.md that was true when written and was never retired when the work it described completed.
findings.fix: Rewrite CLAUDE.md:529-530 to past tense with the current state: "M13-16 landed the first frontend CI job (`frontend-tests`: npm ci -> jest --ci -> eslint src -> tsc --noEmit) non-blocking to measure the red count; **the ratchet completed and all three steps are BLOCKING at HEAD** — the only `continue-on-error` steps remaining in ci.yml are the black whole-repo drift report and npm audit." Better still, fold this into finding 04's archive move: the M13-W4 block is a closed wave (L526-531) and belongs in docs/SESSION_BUNDLES.md, with only the live CI-gate summary staying in CLAUDE.md — a closed-wave narrative kept in an always-on file is precisely how this claim outlived its truth.

findings.title: P3 sweep — nine smaller config/doc defects across CLAUDE.md, settings.local.json, the pre-commit hook and .mcp.json
findings.evidence: (1) CLAUDE.md:424 "~557 test files" — actual `ls tests/test_*.py | wc -l` = 587 at HEAD. (2) CLAUDE.md:227 "`tests/test_security_regression.py` (~98 tests)" — actual `grep -c 'def test_'` = 104. (3) CLAUDE.md:17 pins "MEASURED 2026-09-01: 43 vulnerabilities (1 low, 20 moderate, 21 high, 1 critical)" as an App-Store gate input; baseline/README.txt measured 2026-09-05 after a fresh `npm ci` gives 42 (1 low, 21 moderate, 19 high, 1 critical) — a hand-pinned count that has already drifted, on a gate. (4) .githooks/pre-commit has no equivalent of CI's "Lock is current" step (ci.yml:32-46), so an edit to requirements.in committed without `uv pip compile` passes the hook and fails CI — CLAUDE.md:77 already warns the CI step exists, so the gap is known but unhooked; a 3-line staged-file check for `requirements*.in` without `requirements*.txt` would close it. (5) settings.local.json holds 41 git entries fully subsumed by `Bash(git *)` and 6 python entries subsumed by `Bash(python:*)`, plus `Bash(timeout 100 bash:*)` subsumed by `Bash(timeout:*)` — ~48 of 192 entries are dead weight. GET .../workflows/live-suite.yml/runs -> `total 1` : run 33382901180, sha a05a4f0, schedule, conclusion=failure, 2026-08-31. Its job log (99459017272, step 5): `ERROR tests/test_two_input_shape.py - openai.OpenAIError: Missing credentials. Please pass an api_key ... or set the OPENAI_API_KEY` repeated, then `!!! Interrupted: 89 errors during collection !!!` and `14100 deselected, 1 warning, 89 errors in 31.81s`, `Process completed with exit code 2`. Issue #96 ('Live adapter suite failed - likely scraper drift') is the auto-opened report and is still open.
findings.repro:
TOK=$(printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com

'|git credential fill|sed -n 's/^password=//p'); curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" https://api.github.com/repos/KGRddhs/smartcompare-backend/actions/secrets ; curl -sL -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" https://api.github.com/repos/KGRddhs/smartcompare-backend/actions/jobs/99459017272/logs | grep -a 'errors during collection'
findings.impact: Zero adapter-drift coverage. The workflow header says 37 live_unit nodes are the ONLY automated channel that exercises the runtime adapter path against real storefronts; 0 of them have ever run. A retailer changing its markup is still detected by a user, not by CI - which is the exact gap #49 built this workflow to close. Worse than #96 records: it is not one missing secret, it is ALL SIX (OPENAI_API_KEY, SERPER_API_KEY, FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, SCRAPEDO_API_TOKEN, ZYTE_API_KEY, BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY resolve to ''), so setting OPENAI alone gets past collection and then fails every adapter node on an unauthenticated vendor call. It also means the workflow's own PRODUCTION-CACHE AUDIT (Layer 1/Layer 2) has never been exercised in practice.
findings.fix: Two parts. (a) Make the failure legible instead of a 89-error collection wall: add a guard step before pytest that fails fast with an explicit message when any of the six vendor secrets is empty (`[ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ] || { echo '::error::OPENAI_API_KEY secret is unset - live-suite cannot run'; exit 1; }`), and pin it with a new test_ci_gates node so the guard cannot be dropped. (b) Populate the six repo secrets (owner action) - and until they exist, either disable the cron or leave it failing loudly; do NOT quietly relax it. No feature flag involved. Note the collection wall is a second, independent defect: openai_service.py:32 builds AsyncOpenAI at MODULE IMPORT, so an empty key breaks collection of 89 files rather than skipping 89 tests - making that construction lazy (as get_client already is) would turn this into a normal skip.
findings.test_first: A new tests/test_ci_gates.py node asserting the live-suite job's first step is a secret-presence guard naming all six vendor keys, plus an assertion that no pytest step in live-suite.yml runs before it. Red today (no guard step exists).

findings.title: The only test covering _update_behavior_profile mocks two columns Postgres does not have, so it can never catch the live 42703 that kills personalization
findings.evidence: tests/test_behavior_integration.py:164 `mock_comparisons = MagicMock(data=[{"category_used": "electronics", "created_at": "2026-03-22T00:00:00"}])` and :166 `mock_events = MagicMock(data=[{"event_type": "tab_switch", "metadata": {...}}])`. The production reads at 76ace90 are structured_comparison_service.py:4545 `.table("comparisons").select("category_used, products, created_at")` and :4547 `.table("user_events").select("event_type, metadata")`. Live read-only Supabase probe (service key, SELECT col LIMIT 1): `MISSING comparisons.category_used -> {'message': 'column comparisons.category_used does not exist', 'code': '42703'}`, same for comparisons.products and user_events.metadata; comparisons.full_response / user_id / created_at and user_events.event_type all resolve OK.
findings.impact: Two of the three reads in `_update_behavior_profile` raise 42703 on every real invocation; the bare `except Exception` at structured_comparison_service.py:4550 swallows it into one WARNING, so `users.behavior_profile` is never written and the behavioural layer of the three-layer personalization (behavioral +/-10%) is permanently dead in production for every user - while ENABLE_COHORT_PERSONALIZATION=true on Railway advertises personalization as on. The test defect is what let it survive M13 and M18: the mock hands back exactly the shape production cannot produce, so the suite reports green. It is now doubly blind - #115 added `.limit(200)` to the feedback read, so the mock's `.select().eq().execute()` chain no longer matches production's `.select().eq().limit().execute()` and MagicMock silently auto-creates a stand-in whose `.data` is a MagicMock; `build_behavior_profile` is itself mocked, so nothing at all is asserted about the retrieved rows.
findings.fix: Replace the shape-fabricating mock with a schema-anchored fake: assert the exact `.select(...)` string the code passes and validate every column name in it against a single committed schema manifest generated from migrations/*.sql (or, better, against the live information_schema in a live_db-marked test), so a `.select()` naming a column no table has fails at commit time. Add a red test that makes the mocked `.execute()` raise APIError 42703 and asserts `_update_behavior_profile` surfaces it (Sentry / a non-debug log) instead of swallowing it - the swallow is what made a dead feature look alive. Fix the product side under the existing #65; no new flag needed since the reads are already best-effort.
findings.test_first: tests/test_behavior_integration.py: (1) `test_update_behavior_profile_selects_only_real_columns` - parse every column out of the three `.select()` calls the code makes and assert each is present in a schema manifest derived from migrations/*.sql; RED today on category_used, products, metadata. (2) `test_update_behavior_profile_reports_a_postgrest_error` - make execute() raise a 42703 APIError and assert it is captured, not debug-logged.
findings.dedupe: known:#65 still-open for the product defect (confirmed at HEAD against the LIVE schema); the TEST defect - a mock that fabricates the phantom shape and a chain that no longer matches production after #115 - is new

findings.title: The Pydantic models that would validate the API response shape are at 0% CI coverage and imported by nothing - there is no schema to catch a wrong-shape payload or a wrong-shape mock
findings.evidence: Measured CI coverage table for 76ace90 (backend-tests job log): `app/models/product_schema.py 104 104 0% 4-167`, `app/models/schemas.py 86 86 0% 4-170`, `app/config.py 24 24 0% 5-55`. Grep for importers across app/ tests/ scripts/ returns only PROSE: response_builder.py:230 '(app/models/product_schema.py:140) is never applied to this dict', tests/test_response_builder_winner_card_consistency.py:327 'ComparisonResult (app/models/product_schema.py:140) is never', plus test-only imports of the separate app.models.scoring_v2. No `from app.models.schemas import` or `from app.models.product_schema import` anywhere in app/.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'app.models' app/ tests/ scripts/ --include=*.py | grep -v '^app/models/'   # only comments + app.models.scoring_v2 ; and grep -a 'app/models' on the CI job log shows both files at 0%
findings.impact: 190 statements of declared API contract are dead. Every response the backend emits is a hand-built dict validated by nothing, which is the structural reason the wrong-shape-mock class of defect (findings 02 and 07, and the already-fixed referral `response_data` breakage) is undetectable by construction: a test can assert any key it likes because no model says which keys exist. It also means the 86%/85.84% coverage headline is computed over a denominator that includes 190 statements which can never be covered, and that `ComparisonResult` - the thing M20's winner-index normalization exists to compensate for - is documented in two places as 'never applied'.
findings.fix: Decide and act, do not leave it ambiguous. Either (a) DELETE app/models/schemas.py and app/models/product_schema.py in one commit (they are 0% covered and zero-imported; deletion also removes 190 uncoverable statements from the coverage denominator and is the honest reading of 'never applied'), or (b) WIRE ComparisonResult as a response_model / a `.model_validate()` at the single `build_comparison_response` exit and let it fail loudly in dev - behind a flag such as ENABLE_RESPONSE_SCHEMA_VALIDATION (default OFF) if the payload is expected to deviate today, so a canary measures the deviation before it blocks. Do (a) unless someone commits to (b) with an owner.
findings.test_first: tests/test_response_schema_contract.py::test_build_comparison_response_validates_against_ComparisonResult - `ComparisonResult.model_validate(build_comparison_response(...))` over a recorded tests/fixtures/comparison_baseline_d2*.json payload. Red today (the model has never been applied); its failure output is the exact list of contract drift.

findings.title: All 245 jest suites run against a 143-line hand-written react-native facsimile with Platform.OS hardcoded to 'ios', so every Android branch in the app is untested
findings.evidence: jest.config.js moduleNameMapper: `'^react-native$': '<rootDir>/__mocks__/react-native.ts'` (plus 19 more wholesale module substitutions). `wc -l __mocks__/react-native.ts` = 143. Inside it: `export const Platform = { OS: 'ios', select: (obj: any) => obj.ios };` (:70), `export const Dimensions = { get: () => ({ width: 390, height: 844, scale: 2, fontScale: 1 }) }` (:72-74), `export const I18nManager = { isRTL: false, ... }` (:87). src carries 17 `Platform.OS`/`Platform.select` uses across 13 files, e.g. `src/services/authService.ts:630  if (Platform.OS !== 'ios') return false;`. Only 2 test files ever override Platform.OS (__tests__/playInstallReferrerService.test.ts and .edges.test.ts).
findings.repro: cd SmartCompareApp && sed -n '70p' __mocks__/react-native.ts && grep -rn "Platform.OS\|Platform.select" src App.tsx | wc -l && grep -rln "Platform" __tests__ | xargs grep -l "Platform.OS =" | wc -l
findings.impact: '2320 jest tests pass / 242 suites green' - which CI now BLOCKS on - is a statement about a stub, not about React Native. Concretely: 15 of the 17 Platform branches only ever take the iOS side, so the Android path of `authService.ts:630` (Apple-Sign-In availability) and 12 other files is executed by no test, on a product that ships to Google Play ('Teen' rating, adaptive-icon.png). `Dimensions` is pinned to one 390x844 device, so no small-screen or tablet layout path is exercised; `I18nManager.isRTL` defaults false and is only flipped by hand in a few primitives tests (DirectionalIcon, SlideTransition), which is the real limit behind the CLAUDE.md claim that the RTL sweep is 'jest-proven in both directions'. Any drift between the stub's shape and the real RN API is invisible until a device sees it - the same failure class as the backend wrong-shape mocks.
findings.fix: Two steps, neither large. (1) Parameterise the platform: export `Platform` from the mock as a mutable object and add a shared test helper `withPlatform('android', fn)`; then add an Android pass over the 13 Platform-touching files (a jest project matrix - two `projects` entries in jest.config.js differing only in a setup file that sets Platform.OS - runs the whole suite twice for ~2x CI minutes and is the cheapest honest fix). (2) Add a contract test that asserts every named export the app imports from 'react-native' exists on the mock, driven by grepping `from 'react-native'` across src - so a new RN import silently resolving to undefined fails in CI instead of at runtime. No app flag.
findings.test_first: __tests__/mocks/reactNativeMock.contract.test.ts - collect every identifier imported from 'react-native' anywhere in src/ and App.tsx and assert `Object.keys(require('../../__mocks__/react-native'))` covers them; plus a red `authService.appleSignInAvailable` test under Platform.OS='android' asserting the early return.

findings.title: The 5 required status checks are bypassable: branch protection on main has enforce_admins false, strict false and no required review
findings.evidence: REST GET /repos/KGRddhs/smartcompare-backend/branches/main/protection -> HTTP 200: required_status_checks.contexts = [backend-lint, dependency-audit, frontend-typecheck, backend-tests, frontend-tests] with `"strict": false`; `"enforce_admins": {"enabled": false}`; `required_pull_request_reviews` is ABSENT from the response entirely; `required_conversation_resolution: {"enabled": false}`; `required_linear_history: false`. ci.yml:107-112 states the opposite intent in prose: 'until branch protection on main lists backend-lint (and backend-tests) under Require status checks to pass ... a PR can still be merged red'.
findings.repro:
TOK=$(printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com

'|git credential fill|sed -n 's/^password=//p'); curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" https://api.github.com/repos/KGRddhs/smartcompare-backend/branches/main/protection | python -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['required_status_checks']['contexts'],d['required_status_checks']['strict'],d['enforce_admins']['enabled'],'reviews' if 'required_pull_request_reviews' in d else 'NO REVIEW RULE')"
findings.impact: Two real holes. (a) enforce_admins=false means the repo admin - who is the only committer here - can push directly to main and none of the 5 required jobs gate that push; the last 5 CI runs on main are all `event: push`, so this is the normal path, and the checks run AFTER the code is already on the branch Railway deploys from. (b) strict=false means a PR can merge while its base is stale, so the green tick belongs to a commit that was never combined with what main now contains - the classic semantic-conflict merge. Combined with no required review, 'all 5 jobs are REQUIRED' (the standing claim in CLAUDE.md and the M22 brief) overstates what actually blocks a bad change from reaching production.
findings.fix: Repo-admin settings change, not code: enable `enforce_admins` (so the owner's own pushes are gated), enable `strict` (require branches up to date before merging), and set required_pull_request_reviews to at least 1 approving review - or, if a solo maintainer cannot self-approve, keep reviews off but turn on enforce_admins + strict, which are the two that actually change the outcome. Then correct the stale prose at ci.yml:107-112, which still describes the pre-#49 state. Record the settings in a test so a silent rollback is visible: no flag involved.
findings.test_first: tests/test_ci_gates.py::test_branch_protection_is_enforced_for_admins - a live_unit-marked node that GETs branches/main/protection and asserts enforce_admins.enabled is true, strict is true, and the 5 contexts are present. Red today on the first two.

findings.title: Re-engagement reads two more columns Postgres does not have, and both are mocked into existence by the tests that cover them
findings.evidence: reengagement_service.py:236-238 `.table("product_reviews").select("sentiment_score")`; live probe -> `MISSING product_reviews.sentiment_score -> {'code': '42703'}`. scripts/cron_reengagement.py:46 `.table("users").select("id, expo_push_token, last_comparison_at, governorate, preferences")`; live probe -> `MISSING users.governorate -> {'code': '42703'}` while the other four columns all resolve OK - i.e. the whole eligible-user query fails on one bad name. The covering tests fabricate both shapes: tests/test_reengagement_internals.py:83 `data=[{"sentiment_score": 0.72}]` asserting `_compute_current_sentiment('p1') == 0.72`, and tests/test_reengagement_service.py:224 `user = {"id": "u", "governorate": "Capital", ...}`. Both call sites swallow the exception (`except Exception ... logger.warning`), so the failure is a log line, not an error.

findings.impact: The frontend half of the product - 2320 tests, 242 suites, and the screens that carry the M21 mobile fixes - has no measured coverage number and no floor, so a PR can delete every test for a screen and the blocking `frontend-tests` job stays green as long as what remains passes. Nobody can say today what fraction of SmartCompareApp/src is exercised. The asymmetry also makes the repo's coverage story misleading: '85.84%' is a backend-only number that reads as if it described the codebase.

findings.title: P3 sweep: four smaller test/CI-truth defects (real DNS in the blocking job, a stale flaky-exclude, a lock gate that ignores the dev lock, and #128's zero-coverage confirmation)
findings.evidence: (a) REAL DNS IN THE BLOCKING JOB - tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py:126-128 `test_detect_allows_valid_url` POSTs {'url': 'https://amazon.ae/dp/B123'} to /api/v1/url/detect with no mock and no marker; app/utils/url_validator.py:30 does `addr_infos = socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, None)` and :31 catches socket.gaierror (-> blocked -> 400), so on a runner that cannot resolve amazon.ae the assert 200 fails. It PASSED in CI at 76ace90 (8 ms), i.e. it is a live dependency on public DNS inside the blocking backend-tests job, not a hypothetical. Fix: monkeypatch url_validator's resolver, or mark it live_unit. (b) STALE NETWORK_FLAKY_EXCLUDE - scripts/regression_gate_diff.py:56-65 blinds the local gate to 4 node ids on BOTH sides; all four PASS in the 76ace90 CI run (test_price_cache_bust_probe::TestPriceReadBypass x2 PASSED, test_algolia_service::test_fetch_price_happy_path_genuine_bhd PASSED) and the fifth, test_rate_limiting_complete::TestRateLimitCoverage::test_prices_endpoint_rate_limited, now carries @pytest.mark.live_unit (:31) so it can never appear in a free-tier failure set at all - a dead entry. Net: the local gate is blind to 4 nodes that CI does gate. Fix: prune the list and re-derive it only from an observed flake. (c) LOCK GATE MISSES THE DEV LOCK - scripts/regression_gate_diff.py:219 `lock_drift(requirements = REPO_ROOT / 'requirements.txt')` compares only the runtime lock; a drifting pytest / pytest-asyncio / pytest-timeout / black from requirements-dev.txt does not trigger the exit-4 refusal, even though those are exactly the packages that decide what a test run MEANS. Fix: iterate both locks. (d) #128 CONFIRMED AT ZERO COVERAGE - app/services/usage_service.py:129 `refund_anon_comparison_credit`; its single body line 135 is in the CI Missing list for that file (`usage_service.py 279 45 84% ... 135 ...`), it has zero references in the whole test tree and zero callers in app/, so nothing red pins the wiring that ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE depends on. VERIFIED WORKING (no defect, recorded so it is not re-checked): scripts/regression_gate_diff.py's exit-4 off-lock refusal FIRES on this box - `python -m scripts.regression_gate_diff --current <file>` -> EXIT=4, 'REFUSING TO CERTIFY: this environment is OFF-LOCK', 48 packages listed; and .githooks/pre-commit is active here (`git config --get core.hooksPath` = .githooks) and adds two checks CI does NOT have (a staged-diff credential/.env guard, sqlfluff on staged migrations) while lacking everything CI has (coverage floor, lock-freshness, pip-audit, the frontend job, the full suite).
findings.repro: (a) grep -n 'getaddrinfo' app/utils/url_validator.py && sed -n '126,128p' tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py ; (b) grep -a 'test_price_cache_bust_probe\|test_fetch_price_happy_path_genuine_bhd' <76ace90 backend-tests job log> && sed -n '31p' tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py ; (c) sed -n '219p' scripts/regression_gate_diff.py ; (d) grep -rc refund_anon_comparison_credit tests/ app/api/
findings.impact: (a) one live-DNS dependency in a job that gates every merge - a runner-side DNS hiccup reddens main for a reason unrelated to the change, which is the flake class the gate exists to avoid. (b) the local regression gate reports 'no regression' for 4 nodes it never looks at, so a dev's green gate is 4 nodes narrower than CI's. (c) a dev on a drifting pytest can get a green certification the exit-4 guard was built to refuse - the guard's own docstring names framework-shape drift as the reason it exists. (d) hard precondition for ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE with no red test behind it.

(c) change lock_drift to accept a sequence of lock files and pass both requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt. (1) Function-level repro (scratchpad/m22-review/cr_sec_03_unit.py, imports the real _before_send by file path): 17 surviving sentinel sites across message, logentry, extra, contexts, user, request.cookies, request.data, request.url, request.query_string and all frame vars. (3) Full-pipeline repro through the REAL runtime path (cr_sec_03_probe.py: real init_sentry() + capturing transport + FastAPI TestClient + the real app.api.admin_routes.verify_admin_key): one unauthenticated request with a raw 0xE9 byte in X-Admin-Key returns HTTP 500 and emits an event carrying 99 sentinel sites, including the production ADMIN_API_KEY verbatim at .exception.values[0].stacktrace.frames[19].vars.expected, the caller JWT at .request.data.access_token, and JWT+session cookie repeated in raw ASGI header tuples across 20 frames. One caveat on the fix as written: adding the bare fragment `key` to _SENSITIVE_KEY_FRAGMENTS will redact benign keys (cache_key, key_features, keywords) across breadcrumbs and extra — prefer `admin_key`/`api-key`/`_key` over `key`.
